definition_zh: 额外的；外加的；额外的东西；附加费用；额外地；特别地；特级的
definition_en: more than is usual, expected, or needed, or something added beyond the usual amount
core_image: 一只已经装满的箱子，上面又绑着一个小包
scene: 结账时，账单上多出一项费用。At the hotel, the bill included an extra charge for breakfast.
sceneCN: 这里 extra 是「额外的」（第 1 个义项：超出平常数量或范围的）；句意：在酒店，账单上多了一笔早餐附加费。

pos.zh: 额外的东西；附加项；临时演员

derivatives.zh: 非凡的；特别的，由 extra（在外）加 ordinary（寻常）构成，意为超出寻常
外来的；无关的，与拉丁 exterus（外部的）同源，指来自外部
额外项目；临时演员，extra 的复数名词化用法

senses.title: Beyond the usual amount
senses.definition: more than the usual, expected, or necessary amount
senses.definitionCN: 超出平常、预期或必要数量的
senses.example: The room charge covers one night, and breakfast is extra.
senses.exampleCN: 房费含一晚，早餐另算。
senses.why: Latin extra means outside or beyond, so the adjective marks what lies outside the agreed amount.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 extra 意为「在外、超出」，所以这个形容词标记的是超出既定数量的部分。

senses.title: An added item or charge
senses.definition: an additional item, charge, or feature supplied beyond what is standard
senses.definitionCN: 在标准配置之外额外提供的东西、费用或功能
senses.example: The holiday price includes taxes and there are no hidden extras.
senses.exampleCN: 度假价格含税，没有隐藏的附加费用。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the added thing itself, and the plural extras names small additions on a bill or in a package.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转化为名词，指被加上去的东西本身；复数 extras 则指账单或套餐里那些小额附加项。

senses.title: To a greater degree
senses.definition: in a greater degree than usual, or especially
senses.definitionCN: 以超过平常的程度，或表示「特别」
senses.example: She worked extra hard before the final exam.
senses.exampleCN: 期末考前她格外用功。
senses.why: As an adverb, extra raises the degree of the action or quality it modifies, pushing it past the normal level.
senses.whyCN: 作副词时，extra 抬升所修饰的动作或性质的程度，把它推到平常水平之上。

senses.title: A performer in a crowd
senses.definition: a person who appears in a film or play in a minor, usually silent role, often as part of a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 在电影或戏剧中出镜的小角色，通常没有台词，常充当人群的一部分
senses.example: Dozens of extras waited on set for the market scene.
senses.exampleCN: 几十名临时演员在片场等待拍摄集市场景。
senses.why: In theatre and film, an extra is literally an added body beyond the named cast.
senses.whyCN: 在戏剧和电影里，临时演员就是主要演员之外「额外加上」的人。

senses.title: A top trade grade
senses.definition: used before a grade word to mean of the very highest quality
senses.definitionCN: 用在等级词之前，表示质量达到最高等级
senses.example: The mill sells flour graded extra fine for pastry.
senses.exampleCN: 这家磨坊出售标为特级细质的面粉，适合做糕点。
senses.why: Trade labels use extra to mark goods that go beyond the standard grade.
senses.whyCN: 商品标签用 extra 标记那些超出标准等级的货物。

intro.en: Extra comes from Latin extra, meaning outside or beyond, a form related to exterus, outer.
intro.cn: extra 来自拉丁语 extra（在外、超出），与 exterus（外部的）同族。

items.en: Exterus means outer or outward.
items.cn: exterus 意为外部的、向外的。

items.en: Extra means outside, beyond, or except.
items.cn: extra 意为在外、超出或除……之外。

items.en: The element ex- carries the sense of out.
items.cn: 其中 ex- 这个成分带有「向外」的意思。

items.en: Extra- appears in English compounds as a prefix meaning outside.
items.cn: extra- 在十七世纪英语中作前缀，表示「在外」。

items.en: Extra becomes a standalone adjective meaning additional.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，extra 独立成形容词，表示「额外的」。

items.en: Modern English uses extra for bills, grades, and film crowds.
items.cn: 现代英语把 extra 用在账单、等级和电影人群场景中。

note.en: Extra is a Latin outside word, close to exterior and external, and to everyday words for something added.
note.cn: extra 是拉丁语中表示「外面」的词，与 exterior、external 以及日常表示「附加」的词相邻。

entries.definition: the outer part or surface of something
entries.definitionCN: 外部；外表（与 extra 同出拉丁 exterus）

entries.definition: on, from, or connected with the outside
to take or pull something out
entries.definitionCN: 提取；拔出（只是拼写与 extra 相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: added to what already exists
kept in reserve and available if needed
more than what is needed or used

normalIntro.en: Extra is the outside portion: the part that sits beyond the usual pack, price, or cast.
normalIntro.cn: extra 是「外面那一份」：超出常规包装、价格或演员表的那部分。

normal.en: Extra starts with ex-, the Latin sign for out.
normal.cn: extra 以 ex- 开头，拉丁语里表示「向外」。

normal.en: An extra charge is added outside the basic price.
normal.cn: extra charge 是在基础价格之外加上的费用。

normal.en: Go the extra mile means to do more than required.
normal.cn: go the extra mile 意为比要求的多做一点。

normal.en: In a film, extras fill the background beyond the named cast.
normal.cn: 在电影里，extras 是主要演员之外填补背景的人。

normal.en: Compare additional: additional is neutral, while extra often hints at something beyond the expected.
normal.cn: 对比 additional：additional 较中性，extra 常暗示超出预期。

abstract.en: Picture a full suitcase with a small bag strapped on top.
abstract.cn: 想象一只装满的箱子，上面又绑了一个小包。

abstract.en: Imagine a receipt with one line added below the total.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据，总价下面又多出一行。

abstract.en: See a runner taking one more step past the finish line.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者越过终点线后又多跑一步。

examples.en: The hotel charges extra for parking.
examples.cn: 酒店停车另外收费。

examples.en: She packed an extra pair of shoes for the trip.
examples.cn: 她为旅行多带了一双鞋。

examples.en: The director hired fifty extras for the crowd scene.
examples.cn: 导演为人群场景雇了五十名临时演员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱克斯抓」——多出来的东西就一把「抓」在手里；纯粹谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ exterus（外部的）→ extra（在外、超出）→ 英语 extra（额外的；额外之物）。核心是「超出常规的那一部分」。

sensesIntro.en: Extra begins as the outside position beyond an agreed amount, then names the added item, the higher degree, the minor performer, and the top trade grade.
sensesIntro.cn: extra 从「超出既定数量之外」的位置出发，进而指加上去的东西、更高的程度、次要的演员以及最高的商品等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a full case with one small bag tied on top.
core.cn: 核心意象：装满的箱子上面又绑了一个小包。

branches.en: The adjective marks what lies beyond the usual amount.
branches.cn: 形容词义标记超出平常数量的部分。

branches.en: The noun names the added item itself.
branches.cn: 名词义指被加上去的东西本身。

branches.en: The adverb raises the degree of an action.
branches.cn: 副词义抬升动作的程度。

branches.en: A film extra is an added body beyond the named cast.
branches.cn: 电影临时演员是主要演员之外额外加上的人。

branches.en: Both a surplus charge and a top grade sit beyond the standard.
branches.cn: 附加费用与特级品质都处在标准之外。

intro.en: Extra is built from the Latin prefix ex- and the root exterus, and English words such as extraordinary and extraneous belong to its wider family.
intro.cn: extra 由拉丁语前缀 ex- 与词根 exterus 构成，英语的 extraordinary 与 extraneous 也属于这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex- means out, and exterus means outer; extra joins the two ideas into outside or beyond.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ex- 表示「向外」，exterus 表示「外部的」；extra 把两层意思合成「在外、超出」。

items.example: The prefix ex- points outward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 指向外。

items.example: Exterus describes what lies outside.
items.exampleCN: exterus 描述位于外部的东西。

items.example: Extra marks a position beyond a boundary.
items.exampleCN: extra 标记边界之外的位置。

items.example: The prefix extra- forms extraterrestrial.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 extra- 构成 extraterrestrial。

items.example: Extraordinary means beyond the ordinary.
items.exampleCN: extraordinary 意为超出寻常。

items.example: Extraneous material lies outside the main subject.
items.exampleCN: extraneous 指来自主题之外的素材。

items.example: The bill lists several extras.
items.exampleCN: 账单上列了几项额外费用。

items.example: Extra time is added beyond the usual limit.
items.exampleCN: 额外时间是在通常时限之外加上的。

items.example: The package comes with two extras.
items.exampleCN: 这个套餐附赠两样额外的东西。

definition_zh: 提取；拔出；摘录；提炼；提取物
definition_en: to draw or take something out of a place, a source, or a text
core_image: 双手握钳，把嵌进木板里的钉子一点点拔出来
scene: 牙医检查后决定，这颗坏牙不能再留，必须整颗取出。The dentist had to extract the damaged tooth before the gum could heal.
sceneCN: 这里 extract 是「拔出、取出」（第 1 个义项：把嵌住的东西拉出来）；句意：牙医必须先把坏牙拔掉，牙龈才能愈合。

derivatives.zh: 由动词 extract 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「提取；拔除；摘录」
由 extract 加表示器具或施动者的后缀 -or 构成，义为「提取器；抽风机」
由 extract 加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「提取的；采掘的」
由 extract 加 -able 构成，义为「可提取的；可拔出的」

senses.title: To pull something out
senses.definition: to draw or pull something out of a place where it is fixed or enclosed
senses.definitionCN: 把固定在或包在里面的东西拉出来
senses.example: She had to have a cracked molar extracted last week.
senses.exampleCN: 她上周不得不拔掉一颗裂开的臼齿。
senses.why: Latin ex- means out and trahere means to pull, so the word pictures one outward tug.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 ex- 表示「向外」，trahere 表示「拉」，所以这个词画的是一个往外拽的动作。

senses.title: To obtain information or data
senses.definition: to take particular information or values out of a larger body of data or a source
senses.definitionCN: 从更大的数据体或来源中取出特定的信息或数值
senses.example: The tool extracts every email address from the file.
senses.exampleCN: 这个工具会从文件里提取每一个电子邮箱地址。
senses.why: The same outward pull turns abstract: useful pieces are drawn out of a mass of material.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「往外拉」的动作变得抽象：有用的碎片被从一大堆材料里抽出来。

senses.title: To quote a passage from a text
senses.definition: to choose and copy a short passage from a book, speech, or document
senses.definitionCN: 从书、演讲或文件中挑出一段并抄录下来
senses.example: He extracted two sentences from the report for his essay.
senses.exampleCN: 他从报告里摘录了两句话放进自己的文章。
senses.why: Pulling a passage out of a long text is the same gesture applied to words instead of objects.
senses.whyCN: 从长文里抽出一段，是同一个「抽出来」的动作，只是对象从实物换成了文字。

senses.title: To draw out a substance
senses.definition: to get oil, juice, or another substance out of a raw material by pressure or a chemical process
senses.definitionCN: 用压榨或化学方法从原料中取得油、汁液等物质
senses.example: The factory extracts sugar from the beet pulp.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂从甜菜渣里提炼糖。
senses.why: Pressing or dissolving raw material forces the valuable part out, an industrial version of the same pull.
senses.whyCN: 压榨或溶解原料，是把有价值的部分逼出来，这是同一种「拉出」的工业版本。

senses.title: A chosen passage
senses.definition: a short piece of writing taken from a longer work
senses.definitionCN: 从较长作品中取出的一小段文字
senses.example: The anthology prints an extract from her novel.
senses.exampleCN: 这本选集印了她小说的一段摘录。
senses.why: The noun names the thing that has been pulled out of the larger text.
senses.whyCN: 名词指的就是那个已经从整篇文字里被抽出来的东西。

senses.title: A concentrated substance
senses.definition: a thick liquid or powder in which the essential part of a plant or food is concentrated
senses.definitionCN: 把植物或食物的精华浓缩其中而得到的浓液或粉末
senses.example: Add a spoon of vanilla extract to the batter.
senses.exampleCN: 往面糊里加一勺香草精。
senses.why: What has been drawn out of the raw material becomes a product with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 从原料里被抽出来的那一部分，最后成了有自己名字的产品。

intro.en: Extract goes back to Latin ex-, out, and trahere, to draw or pull, which combine in extrahere, to draw out.
intro.cn: extract 可追到拉丁语 ex-（向外）与 trahere（拉、拽），两者合成 extrahere（拉出来）。

items.en: Trahere means to draw, pull, or drag something along.
items.cn: trahere 意为拉、拽、拖动。

items.en: The prefix ex- adds the idea of movement out of something.
items.cn: 前缀 ex- 加上「从某物中出来」的意思。

items.en: Extrahere joins the two into one verb meaning to draw out.
items.cn: extrahere 把两者合成一个动词，意为拉出来。

items.en: The participle extractus means drawn out and also names what has been drawn out.
items.cn: 分词 extractus 意为被拉出来的，也指被拉出来的东西。

items.en: Old French borrows the Latin verb and passes a shortened form toward English.
items.cn: 古法语借入这个拉丁动词，并把简化的形式传向英语。

items.en: English keeps the verb and later adds the noun for passages and concentrated substances.
items.cn: 英语保留了动词，后来又加上名词用法，指选段与浓缩物。

note.en: Extract belongs to the trahere family and overlaps with words for removing and for quoted passages.
note.cn: extract 属于 trahere 家族，并与表示「移走」和「摘录」的词义域相邻。

entries.definition: the act or result of extracting something
entries.definitionCN: 提取；拔除；摘录（动作或结果）

entries.definition: a machine or person that extracts something
to pull someone or something toward oneself
entries.definitionCN: 吸引；拉向自己（与 extract 同出 trahere「拉」）

entries.definition: to take something away from a place
a short piece taken from a longer text
to pull something back or out

normalIntro.en: Extract is a pulling-out word: ex- pushes outward and trahere supplies the pull.
normalIntro.cn: extract 是一个「往外拉」的词：ex- 表示向外，trahere 提供「拉」的动作。

normal.en: Break it as ex- plus tract: tract carries the pulling.
normal.cn: 拆成 ex- 加 tract：tract 带着「拉」的意思。

normal.en: Extraction is the noun for the act.
normal.cn: extraction 是表示这一动作的名词。

normal.en: You extract a tooth, data, or a quotation.
normal.cn: 你可以拔牙、提取数据，也可以摘录引文。

normal.en: Vanilla extract is the flavour drawn out of the bean.
normal.cn: vanilla extract 是从香草豆里抽出来的香味成分。

normal.en: An extract in a book is a passage pulled from a longer text.
normal.cn: 书里的 extract 是从长文中抽出来的一段。

abstract.en: Picture a nail held tight by wood and slowly drawn out.
abstract.cn: 想象钉子被木头紧紧咬住，再被慢慢拔出来。

abstract.en: Imagine a miner picking one bright grain out of a heap of sand.
abstract.cn: 想象矿工从一堆沙里拣出一粒亮晶晶的矿粒。

abstract.en: See a hand copying one paragraph out of a thick book.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从厚书里抄下一段文字。

examples.en: The team extracted the key figures from the survey.
examples.cn: 团队从调查中提取了关键数据。

examples.en: The magazine printed an extract from her new novel.
examples.cn: 杂志刊登了她新小说的一段摘录。

examples.en: Oil is extracted from the seeds by pressing.
examples.cn: 油是通过压榨从种子里提炼出来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex 加 tract」读起来像「一次拽」——一次就把东西拽出来，正是提取；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ trahere（拉、拽）→ extrahere（拉出来）→ 英语 extract；核心义「把里面的东西往外拉」。

sensesIntro.en: Extract moves from pulling a solid object out, to drawing out data, to quoting a passage, and then to the named passage and the concentrated substance.
sensesIntro.cn: extract 从把实物拉出来，扩展到抽出数据、摘录文字，最后指摘出来的段落和浓缩出来的物质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand drawing a nail out of a wooden board.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把钉子从木板里拔出来。

branches.en: Pulling a fixed object out is the physical core.
branches.cn: 把固定的物体拉出来，是这个词的物理核心。

branches.en: Data is drawn out of a larger source.
branches.cn: 数据是从更大的来源里抽出来的。

branches.en: Words are drawn out of a longer text.
branches.cn: 文字是从更长的文本里抽出来的。

branches.en: A substance is forced out of raw material.
branches.cn: 物质是被从原料里逼出来的。

branches.en: The passage and the concentrate are both things that have been drawn out.
branches.cn: 摘录与浓缩物都是已经被抽出来的东西。

intro.en: Extract is built from the Latin prefix ex- and the root trahere, and English adds a whole family around it.
intro.cn: extract 由拉丁语前缀 ex- 与词根 trahere 构成，英语围绕它长出一整族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex- means out, trahere means to pull, and extrahere means to draw out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ex- 意为向外，trahere 意为拉，extrahere 意为拉出来。

items.example: The prefix ex- marks movement outward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 标记向外的移动。

items.example: Trahere supplies the pulling image.
items.exampleCN: trahere 提供「拉」的意象。

items.example: The root tract- appears in many English words.
items.exampleCN: 词根 tract- 出现在许多英语词里。

items.example: Extrahere joins the prefix and the verb.
items.exampleCN: extrahere 把前缀和动词合在一起。

items.example: Extractus is the participle behind the English word.
items.exampleCN: extractus 是英语词背后的分词形式。

items.example: Extract keeps the Latin sense.
items.exampleCN: extract 保留了拉丁语的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms extraction.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成 extraction。

items.example: The suffix -or forms extractor for a device.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 构成表示器具的 extractor。

items.example: The suffix -able forms extractable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 extractable。

definition_zh: 课外的；课程以外的；课余的；课外活动（常用复数）
definition_en: relating to activities that take place outside the normal school curriculum
core_image: 放学后仍亮着灯的活动室，学生在里面排练戏剧
scene: 学校鼓励学生参加课堂之外的活动。The school encourages students to join extracurricular clubs after class.
sceneCN: 这里 extracurricular 是「课外的」（第 1 个义项：不属于正式课程范围的）；句意：学校鼓励学生课后参加课外社团。

pos.zh: 课外的；课程以外的；课余的
课外活动（常用复数 extracurriculars）

derivatives.zh: 在课外地；以课外活动的方式，由 extracurricular 加副词后缀 -ly 构成
课外活动，形容词加复数 -s 名词化，指各项课余活动

senses.title: Outside the curriculum
senses.definition: outside the normal course of study at a school or college
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或学院正式课程范围之外的
senses.example: The school offers extracurricular music lessons on Fridays.
senses.exampleCN: 学校每周五开设课外音乐课。
senses.why: Extra- means outside and curriculum means course, so the word literally points to what lies outside the course.
senses.whyCN: extra- 表示「在外」，curriculum 表示「课程」，所以这个词字面上就指向课程之外的部分。

senses.title: Beyond formal lessons
senses.definition: connected with interests or duties that are not part of formal academic work
senses.definitionCN: 与不属于正式学业任务的兴趣或事务有关的
senses.example: Her extracurricular reading ranged from poetry to astronomy.
senses.exampleCN: 她的课外阅读从诗歌延伸到天文学。
senses.why: The same outside position can describe any pursuit that sits beyond formal lessons.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「在外」位置也能描述任何处在正式课堂之外的追求。

senses.title: Activities as a plural noun
senses.definition: activities outside the curriculum, especially those that develop skills or character
senses.definitionCN: 课程之外的活动，尤指能够培养技能或品格的那些
senses.example: Colleges look at extracurriculars as well as grades.
senses.exampleCN: 大学既看成绩，也看课外活动。
senses.why: English turns the adjective into a plural noun for the activities themselves.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个形容词转为复数名词，直接指活动本身。

intro.en: Extracurricular joins Latin extra, outside, to curriculum, a course of study, and belongs to modern educational vocabulary.
intro.cn: extracurricular 把拉丁语 extra（在外）与 curriculum（课程）组合起来，属于现代教育词汇。

items.en: Extra means outside or beyond.
items.cn: extra 意为在外、超出。

items.en: Curriculum means a course of study or a racecourse.
items.cn: curriculum 意为课程，也指跑道。

items.en: Currere means to run, and a curriculum is the track one runs.
items.cn: currere 意为跑，curriculum 就是人跑的那条跑道。

items.en: Extra- and curriculum combine in educational writing.
items.cn: extra- 与 curriculum 在教育文献中组合成词。

items.en: Extracurricular covers clubs, sport, music, and volunteering.
items.cn: extracurricular 涵盖社团、体育、音乐与志愿服务。

items.en: The plural extracurriculars names such activities.
items.cn: 复数 extracurriculars 直接指这些活动。

note.en: Extracurricular shares its two Latin parts with curriculum and curricular, and sits near words for out-of-class learning.
note.cn: extracurricular 与 curriculum、curricular 共享两个拉丁语成分，并与表示「课堂之外的学习」的说法相邻。

entries.definition: the subjects taught in a school or course
entries.definitionCN: 课程；教学大纲（extracurricular 的后半部分）

entries.definition: relating to a curriculum
entries.definitionCN: 课程的；与教学大纲有关的

entries.definition: outside the walls of a school, especially for adult learners
entries.definitionCN: 校外的；墙外的（extra- 加拉丁 muros「墙」，构词方式与 extracurricular 相近）

entries.definition: happening after the school day ends
connected with learning that supports the formal curriculum
entries.definitionCN: 与正式课程相配合的学习活动有关的

entries.definition: not related to formal study or scholarship
entries.definitionCN: 非学业的；与正式学习无关的

normalIntro.en: Extracurricular is literally outside the course: extra- plus curriculum.
normalIntro.cn: extracurricular 字面上就是「课程之外」：extra- 加 curriculum。

normal.en: Break the word into extra- (outside) and curriculum (course).
normal.cn: 把词拆成 extra-（在外）与 curriculum（课程）。

normal.en: An extracurricular club meets outside the timetable.
normal.cn: 课外社团在课表之外活动。

normal.en: Extracurricular does not mean unimportant; it means beyond the syllabus.
normal.cn: extracurricular 不代表不重要，它表示「超出教学大纲」。

normal.en: The plural extracurriculars names the activities themselves.
normal.cn: 复数 extracurriculars 直接指这些活动本身。

normal.en: Compare curricular: curricular belongs to the course, extracurricular sits outside it.
normal.cn: 对比 curricular：curricular 属于课程，extracurricular 则在课程之外。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom door with a sign pointing to the garden.
abstract.cn: 想象教室门上有一块牌子，指向花园。

abstract.en: Imagine a student reading astronomy at home while the textbook waits on the desk.
abstract.cn: 想象学生在家读天文学，课本却留在书桌上。

abstract.en: See a wall of posters for chess, choir, and football beside the timetable.
abstract.cn: 想象课表旁边贴满国际象棋、合唱与足球的海报。

examples.en: She balances extracurricular activities with a full academic load.
examples.cn: 她在繁重学业与课外活动之间保持平衡。

examples.en: The scholarship rewards extracurricular involvement as well as grades.
examples.cn: 这项奖学金既看重成绩，也看重课外参与。

examples.en: His extracurriculars include debate, rowing, and orchestra.
examples.cn: 他的课外活动包括辩论、划船和管弦乐队。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「课外」两个字就够：extra 在外，curriculum 是课程，合起来就是课程之外的活动；这是拆词联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 extra（在外、超出）+ curriculum（跑道；课程）→ 英语 extracurricular（课程之外的）。核心是「课程表外的那一圈活动」。

sensesIntro.en: Extracurricular starts as the position outside the course, extends to any non-formal pursuit, and is then used as a plural noun for the activities.
sensesIntro.cn: extracurricular 先指「课程之外」的位置，再扩展到任何非正式学业追求，最后名词化为复数，直接指这些活动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door in the school wall that opens onto a garden of clubs.
core.cn: 核心意象：学校墙上的一扇门，通向社团花园。

branches.en: The adjective marks what lies outside the course.
branches.cn: 形容词义标记课程之外的部分。

branches.en: The same position extends to any non-formal pursuit.
branches.cn: 同一位置延伸到任何非正式的追求。

branches.en: The plural noun names the activities themselves.
branches.cn: 复数名词直接指活动本身。

branches.en: Both senses describe learning that sits beyond formal lessons.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述处于正式课堂之外的学习。

branches.en: Personal pursuits become the activities that schools list and reward.
branches.cn: 个人追求变成学校会列出并奖励的课外活动。

intro.en: Extracurricular is a transparent compound of the prefix extra- and the Latin noun curriculum, with curricular and extramural as nearby formations.
intro.cn: extracurricular 是前缀 extra- 与拉丁名词 curriculum 的透明组合，curricular 与 extramural 是邻近的构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin extra means outside, and curriculum means a course or racecourse, from currere, to run.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extra 意为在外，curriculum 意为课程或跑道，源自 currere（跑）。

items.example: The prefix extra- forms extracurricular.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 extra- 构成 extracurricular。

items.example: Curriculum is the course a school runs.
items.exampleCN: curriculum 就是学校所跑的课程。

items.example: Currere supplies the running image.
items.exampleCN: currere 提供「奔跑」的意象。

items.example: Curricular matters belong to the official course.
items.exampleCN: curricular 事务属于正式课程。

items.example: Extracurricular learning happens beyond lessons.
items.exampleCN: extracurricular 学习发生在课堂之外。

items.example: Extracurriculars enrich school life.
items.exampleCN: 课外活动丰富学校生活。

items.example: Extramural courses reach the wider community.
items.exampleCN: extramural 课程面向更广泛的社区。

items.example: The suffix -ar forms curricular.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ar 构成 curricular。

definition_zh: 引渡；引渡程序；移交逃犯；引渡制度
definition_en: the official legal process of handing over a person accused or convicted of a crime to another country or jurisdiction
core_image: 两名官员在边境口岸把一名戴手铐的人交给对方
scene: 两国签有协议，可以把逃犯送回国受审。The two countries signed a treaty that allows extradition of fugitives.
sceneCN: 这里 extradition 是「引渡」（第 1 个义项：把被指控犯罪的人移交另一国）；句意：两国签署条约，允许引渡逃犯。

pos.zh: 引渡；引渡程序；移交逃犯；引渡制度

derivatives.zh: 引渡，由 extradition 逆构而来的动词，指把被控者移交另一国
可引渡的，由 extradite 加形容词后缀 -able 构成
已被引渡的，extradite 的过去分词作形容词

senses.title: Handing over an accused person
senses.definition: the formal surrender of a person accused or convicted of a crime by one state or authority to another
senses.definitionCN: 一国或一个司法管辖区把被指控或被判犯罪的人正式移交给另一国或另一管辖区
senses.example: The judge approved his extradition to face trial abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 法官批准将他引渡到国外受审。
senses.why: Latin ex- means out and traditio means a handing over, so extradition is a legal handing out of a person to another jurisdiction.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ex- 表示「向外」，traditio 表示「交出」，所以引渡就是把一个人依法交出去、交给另一司法管辖区。

senses.title: The legal process and hearings
senses.definition: the legal proceedings and hearings through which such a surrender is arranged
senses.definitionCN: 为安排这种移交而进行的法律程序与听证
senses.example: The extradition proceedings lasted almost two years.
senses.exampleCN: 引渡程序持续了将近两年。
senses.why: The noun also names the whole procedure, not only the final handover.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也指整套程序，而不只是最后那一次移交。

senses.title: The treaty framework
senses.definition: the system of treaties and laws under which states return fugitives to each other
senses.definitionCN: 各国据以互相送回逃犯的条约与法律体系
senses.example: No extradition arrangement exists between the two states.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个国家之间没有引渡安排。
senses.why: Modern use extends the word to the treaty system that makes the handover lawful.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法把这个词扩展到使移交合法的条约体系。

intro.en: Extradition is generally traced to French legal coinage of the nineteenth century, built from Latin ex-, out, and traditio, a handing over.
intro.cn: 一般认为 extradition 由十九世纪法国法律用语造出，取拉丁语 ex-（向外）与 traditio（交出）。

items.en: Tradere means to hand over or deliver.
items.cn: tradere 意为交出、递出。

items.en: Traditio means a handing over, delivery, or surrender.
items.cn: traditio 意为交出、移交或让渡。

items.en: French legal writers coin extradition from the Latin elements.
items.cn: 法国法律作者用这些拉丁语成分造出 extradition。

items.en: English adopts extradition for international returns of suspects.
items.cn: 英语借用 extradition 来表示跨国送回嫌疑人。

items.en: Treaties make extradition a routine part of international law.
items.cn: 条约使引渡成为国际法的常规部分。

items.en: The word now covers hearings, requests, and whole treaty systems.
items.cn: 这个词现在涵盖听证、请求以及整套条约体系。

note.en: Extradition shares the Latin handing-over root with extradite, extraditable, and tradition, and sits near other legal transfer words.
note.cn: extradition 与 extradite、extraditable、tradition 共享拉丁语「交出」词根，并与其它法律移交词相邻。

entries.definition: to hand a person over to another state for trial
entries.definitionCN: 引渡（动词）：把某人移交给另一国受审

entries.definition: liable to be handed over under an extradition treaty
a custom or belief handed down over time
entries.definitionCN: 传统；世代相传的做法（与 traditio 同源，词义已分化）

entries.definition: the transfer of a person to another authority, sometimes outside formal extradition
entries.definitionCN: 移交；非常规引渡（语义与引渡相近，程序可能不同）

entries.definition: the expulsion of a foreigner from a country
entries.definitionCN: 驱逐出境（针对居留资格，而非刑事移交）

entries.definition: the act of giving oneself or another person up to an authority

normalIntro.en: Extradition is a legal handing over: ex- sends the person out, and traditio is the delivery.
normalIntro.cn: extradition 是一次依法「交出去」：ex- 把人往外送，traditio 是交付。

normal.en: Break extradition into ex- (out) and traditio (a handing over).
normal.cn: 把词拆成 ex-（向外）与 traditio（交出）。

normal.en: An extradition treaty sets the rules for handing a suspect across a border.
normal.cn: 引渡条约规定把嫌疑人送过边境的规则。

normal.en: Extradition is the noun; extradite is the verb; extraditable describes the person.
normal.cn: extradition 是名词，extradite 是动词，extraditable 描述可被引渡的人。

normal.en: The process includes a request, a hearing, and a final handover.
normal.cn: 引渡过程包括请求、听证和最后的移交。

normal.en: Compare deportation: deportation expels a foreigner, extradition returns a suspect to face trial.
normal.cn: 对比 deportation：驱逐出境针对外国人居留，引渡则把嫌疑人送回受审。

abstract.en: Picture two officers meeting at a border gate with a prisoner between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两名官员在边境大门会面，中间站着一名在押者。

abstract.en: Imagine a folder of papers moving through a courtroom before the handover.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠文件在移交前穿过法庭。

abstract.en: See a signed treaty on a desk with a map and two flags.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上放着一份签署的条约，旁边是地图和两面旗。

examples.en: The government filed an extradition request with the neighbouring state.
examples.cn: 政府向邻国提出了引渡请求。

examples.en: He is fighting extradition on the grounds that the evidence is weak.
examples.cn: 他以证据薄弱为由抗拒引渡。

examples.en: The extradition treaty was signed after years of negotiation.
examples.cn: 这项引渡条约经过多年谈判后签署。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一克斯抓地审」——把人「抓」住、递到另一国去审；这是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ traditio（交出、移交，源自 tradere「递出」）→ 法语 extradition → 英语 extradition，核心义「把被控者交出去」。

sensesIntro.en: Extradition names the handover itself, then the legal process that arranges it, and finally the treaty system that authorizes it.
sensesIntro.cn: extradition 先指移交行为本身，再指安排移交的法律程序，最后指授权移交的条约体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a prisoner handed across a border gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一名在押者被送过边境大门。

branches.en: The core sense is the legal handover of an accused person.
branches.cn: 核心义是把被控者依法交出去。

branches.en: The procedure sense covers the hearings that arrange the handover.
branches.cn: 程序义涵盖安排移交的听证过程。

branches.en: The treaty sense names the legal system behind the handover.
branches.cn: 制度义指支撑移交的法律体系。

branches.en: A single extradition needs both a legal decision and a process.
branches.cn: 一次引渡既需要法律决定，也需要程序。

branches.en: The handover is lawful only when a treaty framework allows it.
branches.cn: 只有条约体系允许时，移交才合法。

intro.en: Extradition is built from the Latin prefix ex- and the handing-over root found in tradere and traditio, with English extradite and extraditable derived from it.
intro.cn: extradition 由拉丁语前缀 ex- 与 tradere、traditio 中的「交出」词根构成，英语的 extradite 与 extraditable 由它派生。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex- means out, tradere means to hand over, and traditio means a handing over.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ex- 意为向外，tradere 意为交出，traditio 意为交出、移交。

items.example: The prefix ex- marks movement outward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 标记向外的移动。

items.example: Tradere is the act of handing something over.
items.exampleCN: tradere 就是把手里的东西交出去。

items.example: Traditio supplies the core of extradition.
items.exampleCN: traditio 提供 extradition 的核心含义。

items.example: French extradition names the legal surrender.
items.exampleCN: 法语 extradition 指这种法律上的交出。

items.meaning: the legal handover of a suspect
items.example: English extradition keeps the legal sense.
items.exampleCN: 英语 extradition 保留了这一法律含义。

items.example: To extradite is to surrender a suspect.
items.exampleCN: extradite 就是交出嫌疑人。

items.example: An extraditable offence allows the request.
items.exampleCN: 可引渡的罪行使请求得以成立。

items.example: Tradition shares the handing over image.
items.exampleCN: tradition 共享「交出、传下」的意象。

items.example: The suffix -tion forms action nouns.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tion 构成动作名词。

definition_zh: 无关的；外来的；多余的
definition_en: not belonging to or connected with the subject being considered
core_image: 一株从墙外飘进来的草，长在别人的花圃里
scene: 整理实验记录时，研究员把与课题无关的备注全部划掉。While tidying the lab notes, the researcher crossed out every extraneous remark.
sceneCN: 这里 extraneous 是「无关的」（第 1 个义项：与讨论的主题不相干）；句意：整理实验记录时，研究员把与课题无关的备注全部划掉。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「无关地；以外来的方式」
形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「无关性；外来性」

senses.title: Not connected with the subject
senses.definition: not related to the matter being discussed or considered
senses.definitionCN: 与正在讨论或考虑的事情没有关系
senses.example: The judge ruled that the question was extraneous to the case.
senses.exampleCN: 法官裁定这个问题与本案无关。
senses.why: Extra means outside, so an extraneous remark stands outside the matter at hand.
senses.whyCN: extra 意为「在外面」，所以无关的话就站在当前议题之外。

senses.title: Coming from outside
senses.definition: coming or introduced from outside a thing, group, or system
senses.definitionCN: 从某物、某群体或某系统之外进入的
senses.example: The sample was contaminated by extraneous material from the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 样品被实验台上外来的物质污染了。
senses.why: The Latin source extraneus means foreign, so anything from without is extraneous.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源 extraneus 意为「外来的」，所以从外部来的东西就是外来的。

senses.title: Added and unnecessary
senses.definition: added to something although it is not needed and can be removed
senses.definitionCN: 附加在事物上但并不需要、可以去掉的
senses.example: The editor cut several extraneous details from the report.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑删掉了报告里几处多余的细节。
senses.why: What lies outside the essential content can be stripped away, so the word also means superfluous.
senses.whyCN: 落在核心内容之外的东西可以被剥掉，所以这个词也指「多余的」。

senses.title: A factor outside the design
senses.definition: in research, a factor that comes from outside the experiment and may affect its results
senses.definitionCN: 研究中来自实验之外、可能影响结果的变量
senses.example: The team controlled extraneous variables such as room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 团队控制了室温等无关变量。
senses.why: Scientists name outside factors extraneous because they do not belong to the variable being tested.
senses.whyCN: 科学家把外部因素称为无关变量，因为它们不属于正在检验的变量。

senses.title: Not part of the essence
senses.definition: not belonging to the essential nature of a thing
senses.definitionCN: 不属于事物本质或固有属性的
senses.example: Philosophers separate essential qualities from extraneous ones.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家把本质属性与非本质属性区分开来。
senses.why: The oldest sense of extraneus is simply what is outside, which philosophy applies to non-essential traits.
senses.whyCN: extraneus 最古老的含义就是「在外」，哲学用它来指非本质的特征。

intro.en: Extraneous goes back to Latin extra, outside, and extraneus, external or foreign; English took the adjective from that source.
intro.cn: extraneous 可追溯到拉丁语 extra（在外面）与 extraneus（外部的、外来的），英语直接借入这个形容词。

items.en: Extra means outside or beyond a boundary.
items.cn: extra 意为在外面、超出边界。

items.en: Extraneus is formed on extra and means external or foreign.
items.cn: extraneus 由 extra 构成，意为外部的、外来的。

items.en: The adjective extraneus describes what does not belong to a group or class.
items.cn: 形容词 extraneus 描述不属于某个群体或类别的事物。

items.en: Estrage and estrange develop from the same source and give English strange.
items.cn: estrage 与 estrange 出自同一词源，并进入英语成为 strange。

items.en: Extraneous is recorded in English meaning not belonging to the matter in hand.
items.cn: extraneous 在十七世纪英语中被记录，义为不属于当前事项。

items.en: Modern usage adds extraneous variables in research and extraneous material in science.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了研究中的无关变量与科学中的外来物质。

note.en: Extraneous shares the Latin extra with extra and strange, and stands near irrelevant, extrinsic, and superfluous.
note.cn: extraneous 与 extra、strange 共享拉丁语 extra，并与 irrelevant、extrinsic、superfluous 意义相邻。

entries.definition: added or additional
unfamiliar or unusual
entries.definitionCN: 陌生的；奇怪的（与 extraneous 同出拉丁语 extraneus）

entries.definition: in a way that is not connected with the matter
entries.definitionCN: 无关地；以与主题无关的方式

entries.definition: not connected with the subject
coming from outside rather than from within
more than is needed

normalIntro.en: Extraneous is built from extra, outside, so the word marks whatever stands outside the subject.
normalIntro.cn: extraneous 由 extra（在外面）构成，因此标记一切站在主题之外的东西。

normal.en: Extra plus the adjective ending gives extraneous, literally of the outside.
normal.cn: extra 加上形容词词尾构成 extraneous，字面意思就是「属于外部的」。

normal.en: An extraneous remark is one that has nothing to do with the topic.
normal.cn: extraneous remark 就是与话题毫无关系的话。

normal.en: Scientists remove extraneous material before weighing a sample.
normal.cn: 科学家称量样品前会先去掉外来物质。

normal.en: An extraneous variable comes from outside the experiment and must be controlled.
normal.cn: extraneous variable 来自实验之外，必须加以控制。

normal.en: Compare strange: both words descend from Latin extraneus, one through French.
normal.cn: 对比 strange：两词都出自拉丁语 extraneus，其中一个经由法语传入。

abstract.en: Picture a weed carried over the garden wall into a neat flower bed.
abstract.cn: 想象一株杂草越过院墙落进整齐的花圃。

abstract.en: Imagine a speck of dust settling on a clean glass slide.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒灰尘落在干净的载玻片上。

abstract.en: Think of a page of notes with a paragraph crossed out in red.
abstract.cn: 想象一页笔记上用红笔划掉了一段。

examples.en: The committee ignored the extraneous issue and stayed on the main question.
examples.cn: 委员会忽略了那个无关的问题，继续讨论要点。

examples.en: Wash the equipment to remove extraneous dust.
examples.cn: 清洗设备以除去外来的灰尘。

examples.en: Her essay was strong once the extraneous examples were removed.
examples.cn: 删去多余的例子后，她的文章变得有力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「extra + stray」——额外走失在外的这一份，就是外来的、与本题无关的；这只是读音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 extra（在外面）+ 形容词词尾 -eus／-aneus → extraneus（外部的、外来的）→ 英语 extraneous，核心义「属于外部、不在题内」。同源词 strange 经古法语 estrange 传入。

sensesIntro.en: Extraneous moves from simple outside position to irrelevance, then to needless addition, research variables, and finally non-essential qualities.
sensesIntro.cn: extraneous 从「在外部」这一位置义，延伸到「无关」，再到「多余附加」，又用于研究中的干扰变量，最后指非本质的属性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plant growing outside the wall of the garden.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株长在院墙外的植物。

branches.en: Irrelevance to the matter is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 与主题无关是今天最主要的义项。

branches.en: Physical or social outside origin is the older concrete sense.
branches.cn: 来自外部（物质或群体之外）是更早的具体义项。

branches.en: What comes from outside can often be dropped as superfluous.
branches.cn: 从外部来的东西往往可以当作多余之物去掉。

branches.en: An extraneous variable is irrelevant to the hypothesis yet able to distort it.
branches.cn: 无关变量与假设无关，却能干扰结果。

branches.en: Both foreign origin and non-essential status place a thing outside the core.
branches.cn: 外来的来源与非本质的地位都把事物置于核心之外。

intro.en: Extraneous is extra plus the adjective ending -eous, with English family members built by -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: extraneous 是 extra 加形容词词尾 -eous 构成，英语词族再用 -ly 与 -ness 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin extra means outside, and extraneus, built on it, means external or foreign.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extra 意为在外面，由它构成的 extraneus 意为外部的、外来的。

items.example: The prefix extra- places something outside a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 extra- 把某物置于边界之外。

items.example: Extraneus supplies the whole adjective.
items.exampleCN: extraneus 提供了整个形容词的词干。

items.example: The ending -eous turns a Latin stem into an English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -eous 把拉丁词干变为英语形容词。

items.example: Extraneous keeps the sense of outside origin.
items.exampleCN: extraneous 保留了「来自外部」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb extraneously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 extraneously。

items.example: Extraneously describes an action done without connection.
items.exampleCN: extraneously 描述与主题没有关联的行为。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms the noun extraneousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成名词 extraneousness。

items.example: Extraneousness names the state of lying outside.
items.exampleCN: extraneousness 指处于局外的状态。

items.example: Strange came through French from the same Latin source.
items.exampleCN: strange 经法语来自同一拉丁语源。

items.example: Extra keeps the plain sense of something added.
items.exampleCN: extra 保留「额外添加」的直白含义。

latinEntries.example: Extraneus is the direct Latin ancestor.
latinEntries.exampleCN: extraneus 是直接的拉丁语祖先。

latinEntries.example: Extra is the base of the family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: extra 是整个词族的基座。

latinEntries.example: Exterus belongs to the same outside family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: exterus 属于同一个「外部」词族。

definition_zh: 非凡的；特别的；离奇的
definition_en: very unusual and impressive; much greater than usual; strange and surprising
core_image: 一朵普通花丛中突然开出的巨大奇异花朵
scene: 她展现出非凡的勇气。She showed extraordinary courage.
sceneCN: 这里 extraordinary 是「非凡的、出色的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她展现出非凡的勇气。

derivatives.zh: 非凡地；特别地
非凡；不寻常
普通的；平常的

senses.title: Far beyond usual
senses.definition: much greater or better than usual
senses.definitionCN: 远超过平常水平或质量的
senses.example: She showed extraordinary courage.
senses.exampleCN: 她展现出非凡的勇气。
senses.why: The core sense is standing outside the ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是站在平常之外。

senses.title: Very unusual
senses.definition: very unusual and not happening often
senses.definitionCN: 非常不寻常且不常发生的
senses.example: The team met under extraordinary circumstances.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在特殊情况下开会。
senses.why: Rare events stand outside normal rules.
senses.whyCN: 罕见事件站在常规之外。

senses.title: Strange and surprising
senses.definition: so strange that it surprises people
senses.definitionCN: 奇怪到令人惊讶的
senses.example: He told an extraordinary story about the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲了一个关于大海的离奇故事。
senses.why: The unusual becomes the astonishing.
senses.whyCN: 不寻常变成令人惊异。

intro.en: Extraordinary joins Latin extra, outside, and ordinarius, ordinary.
intro.cn: extraordinary 由拉丁语 extra（在外面）与 ordinarius（普通的）组合而成。

items.en: Extra means outside or beyond.
items.cn: extra 意为在外面或超出。

items.en: Ordinarius means ordinary or usual.
items.cn: ordinarius 意为普通的、通常的。

items.en: The pieces mean outside the ordinary.
items.cn: 两部分合起来意为「超出普通」。

items.en: The word passes through French into English.
items.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语。

items.en: Extraordinary covers greatness and strangeness.
items.cn: 现代英语中 extraordinary 涵盖卓越与离奇。

note.en: Extraordinary is beyond ordinary; ordinary is usual.
note.cn: extraordinary 是超出普通的，ordinary 则是平常的。

entries.definition: not needed or related
spending too much
very great or severe
unusual and worth noticing
much better than usual
not common or ordinary

normalIntro.en: Extraordinary describes what stands far outside the ordinary.
normalIntro.cn: extraordinary 描述远远站在普通之外的事物。

normal.en: She has an extraordinary memory for names.
normal.cn: 她对名字有非凡的记忆力。

normal.en: The rescue was an extraordinary effort.
normal.cn: 这次救援是非凡的努力。

normal.en: They met under extraordinary circumstances.
normal.cn: 他们在特殊情况下会面。

normal.en: The painting is quite extraordinary.
normal.cn: 这幅画相当不寻常。

normal.en: He told an extraordinary tale of survival.
normal.cn: 他讲了一个离奇的生存故事。

abstract.en: Picture one huge flower rising above a plain field.
abstract.cn: 想象一朵巨大的花从普通田野中升起。

abstract.en: Imagine a quiet town where something amazing happens.
abstract.cn: 想象一个安静小镇上发生了惊人的事。

abstract.en: Think of a person who does what no one thought possible.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人做到了大家认为不可能的事。

examples.en: The doctor made an extraordinary effort to save him.
examples.cn: 医生为救他付出了非凡的努力。

examples.en: It was an extraordinary coincidence.
examples.cn: 这是一个离奇的巧合。

examples.en: The team showed extraordinary skill.
examples.cn: 这支队伍展现了非凡的技巧。

dict_mnemonic.text: extra（超出）加 ordinary（普通）：超出普通的，就是 extraordinary（非凡的）。

root: 由拉丁语 extra（超出）与 ordinarius（普通）组合而来，核心义「超出普通、非同寻常」。

sensesIntro.en: Extraordinary means far beyond usual, very unusual, or strange and surprising.
sensesIntro.cn: extraordinary 意为远超平常、非常不寻常，或离奇惊人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one huge flower above a plain field.
core.cn: 核心意象：普通田野上高出一切的一朵巨花。

branches.en: The base sense is greatness beyond the usual.
branches.cn: 基础义是超出平常的卓越。

branches.en: Rare events stand outside normal rules.
branches.cn: 罕见事件站在常规之外。

branches.en: The unusual becomes astonishing.
branches.cn: 不寻常变成令人惊异。

branches.en: Great ability and rare events both exceed the norm.
branches.cn: 卓越能力与罕见事件都超出常规。

branches.en: Special circumstances often produce strange stories.
branches.cn: 特殊情况常常产生离奇故事。

intro.en: Extraordinary is a compound of extra and ordinary, with a large family of related words.
intro.cn: extraordinary 是 extra 与 ordinary 的复合词，拥有一个较大的相关词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin extra and ordinarius are the two source elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extra 与 ordinarius 是两个来源要素。

items.example: The result was extraordinary.
items.exampleCN: 结果非同寻常。

items.example: The team performed extraordinarily well.
items.exampleCN: 团队表现得非常出色。

items.example: The extraordinariness of the event shocked us.
items.exampleCN: 这件事的离奇让我们震惊。

items.example: It was an ordinary day.
items.exampleCN: 那是普通的一天。

items.example: We need an extra chair.
items.exampleCN: 我们需要多一把椅子。

items.example: The report removes extraneous detail.
items.exampleCN: 报告去掉了无关细节。

items.example: The wedding was extravagant.
items.exampleCN: 婚礼很奢侈。

items.example: Ordinarily, the shop closes at six.
items.exampleCN: 商店通常六点关门。

items.example: Extra- marks something beyond.
items.exampleCN: extra- 表示超出。

latinEntries.exampleCN: ordo 是 ordinarius 的词源。

definition_zh: 奢侈；铺张；奢侈品；过度
definition_en: the habit or act of spending much more money than is necessary
core_image: 一桌吃不完的盛宴，剩菜堆成小山
scene: 宴会结束后，账单让东道主自己也吃了一惊。The accountant later called the evening a piece of pure extravagance.
sceneCN: 这里 extravagance 是「奢侈、铺张」（第 1 个义项：花钱远超所需）；句意：宴会结束后，账单让东道主自己也吃了一惊，会计后来把那个晚会称为一场十足的铺张。

collocations.phrase: an extravagance they could not afford

derivatives.zh: 名词词尾 -ance 换为 -ant 构成的同族形容词，义为「奢侈的；夸张的」
同族形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「奢侈地；夸张地」
与词根同源的意大利语形式，义为「华丽的娱乐演出」

senses.title: Spending beyond what is needed
senses.definition: the habit or act of spending far more money than is necessary
senses.definitionCN: 花钱远远超过所需的行为或习惯
senses.example: Few of the guests approved of the wedding extravagance.
senses.exampleCN: 宾客中很少有人赞同这场婚礼的铺张。
senses.why: Extra means outside, so extravagance is money carried outside the bounds of need.
senses.whyCN: extra 意为「在外」，所以奢侈就是把钱花到「需要」的边界之外。

senses.title: An expensive unnecessary thing
senses.titleCN: 奢侈品；昂贵而非必需之物
senses.definition: something costly that is bought even though it is not needed
senses.definitionCN: 价格高昂但并不需要而买下的东西
senses.example: A third car was an extravagance he soon regretted.
senses.exampleCN: 第三辆车是他很快就后悔买下的奢侈品。
senses.why: The count noun names a single item that carries money beyond need.
senses.whyCN: 可数用法指单件物品，它把钱带出了需要的范围。

senses.title: Excess in amount or ornament
senses.definition: an amount or display that is far more than is suitable
senses.definitionCN: 数量或装饰远超适宜程度的展示
senses.example: The hall was built with an extravagance of marble and gold.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅建造时用了过量的大理石与黄金。
senses.why: Once spending is outside limits, the word can name any excessive display.
senses.whyCN: 一旦花费超出限度，这个词就可以指任何过度的展示。

senses.title: Exaggerated speech or feeling
senses.definition: language or emotion that goes beyond what the occasion calls for
senses.definitionCN: 超出场合所需的言辞或情感
senses.example: The speech mixed plain facts with rhetorical extravagance.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇演讲把朴素的事实与修辞上的夸张混在一起。
senses.why: Speech that wanders beyond measure is extravagant in the oldest Latin sense.
senses.whyCN: 言辞一旦漫游到分寸之外，就正是拉丁语最古老意义上的「夸张」。

senses.title: A wild or unreasonable act
senses.definition: an act or claim that departs from what is reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 脱离合理范围的行为或主张
senses.example: The plan was dismissed as an extravagance of the imagination.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划被斥为想象力的荒唐之作。
senses.why: Wandering out of bounds began as a literal image, then came to mean any wild departure.
senses.whyCN: 「游荡出界」最初是字面意象，后来指任何离谱的偏离。

intro.en: Extravagance joins Latin extra, outside, to vagari, to wander, and arrived in English through Italian and French forms.
intro.cn: extravagance 把拉丁语 extra（在外）与 vagari（游荡）结合起来，经意大利语与法语形式进入英语。

items.en: Extra means outside or beyond the limit.
items.cn: extra 意为在外、超出限度。

items.en: Vagari means to wander or roam about.
items.cn: vagari 意为漫游、四处游荡。

items.en: Extravagari means to wander out of bounds.
items.cn: extravagari 意为游荡出界。

items.en: Stravaganza names wildness or excess in behaviour.
items.cn: stravaganza 指行为上的狂放或过度。

items.en: Extravagance reaches English from French in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: extravagance 于十七世纪从法语进入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the money sense and the exaggerated sense.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留花钱过度与夸张两个义项。

note.en: Extravagance keeps the same root as extravagant and shares a family with extravaganza, while sitting near luxury and profligacy.
note.cn: extravagance 与 extravagant 同根，并与 extravaganza 同族，意义上靠近 luxury 与 profligacy。

entries.definition: spending or costing far too much
in an excessive manner
a lavish show or spectacle
great comfort or costly pleasure
reckless and wasteful spending
the habit of using more than is needed

normalIntro.en: Extravagance comes from wandering outside the bounds, so the word pictures money or style that has left the proper track.
normalIntro.cn: extravagance 源自「游荡出界」，所以这个词描绘的是离开了应有轨道的钱财或排场。

normal.en: Extra means outside, so extravagance is spending that has gone outside the limit.
normal.cn: extra 意为在外，所以奢侈就是花到限度之外的钱。

normal.en: The rare verb vagari means to wander, and it gives the second half of the word.
normal.cn: 生僻动词 vagari 意为游荡，它提供了这个词的后半部分。

normal.en: An extravagance can be a single costly item, not only a whole habit.
normal.cn: an extravagance 可以是单件昂贵的东西，而不只是一种习惯。

normal.en: The same root gives the adjective extravagant and the noun extravaganza.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出形容词 extravagant 与名词 extravaganza。

normal.en: Compare luxury: luxury names comfort, extravagance stresses going past what is needed.
normal.cn: 对比 luxury：luxury 指舒适，extravagance 强调超出所需。

abstract.en: Picture a shopping bag carried far past the shop door.
abstract.cn: 想象一只购物袋被拎得远远越过了店门。

abstract.en: Imagine a table crowded with dishes nobody can finish.
abstract.cn: 想象一张堆满菜肴却无人吃得完的桌子。

abstract.en: Think of a hall paved with marble where plain stone would do.
abstract.cn: 想象一间大厅铺满大理石，而普通石头本已够用。

examples.en: Her annual trip to the coast was her one extravagance.
examples.cn: 她每年去海边的那趟旅行是她唯一的奢侈。

examples.en: The council was criticised for the extravagance of the new town hall.
examples.cn: 市议会被批评为新市政厅铺张浪费。

examples.en: He spoke with an extravagance that amused rather than convinced.
examples.cn: 他说话夸张，逗乐了人却没能说服人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「extra + 逛」——读作「额外逛」：额外多逛一圈，钱就铺张出去了；这只是读音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 extra（在外）+ vagari（游荡）→ 晚期拉丁语 extravagari（游荡出界）→ 意大利语 stravaganza → 法语 extravagance → 英语 extravagance，核心义「越出限度的花费或言行」。

sensesIntro.en: Extravagance starts as money spent outside the bounds of need, then names a costly item, an excessive display, exaggerated speech, and finally any wild departure.
sensesIntro.cn: extravagance 先是花到「需要」边界之外的钱，再指昂贵的单品、过度的展示、夸张的言辞，最后指任何离谱的偏离。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a purse carried far beyond the shop door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只钱包被拎得远远越过店门。

branches.en: Overspending on daily life is the central money sense.
branches.cn: 日常开销过度是核心的金钱义项。

branches.en: A single costly purchase is the countable sense.
branches.cn: 单件昂贵的购买是可数义项。

branches.en: Excess in display grows from excess in spending.
branches.cn: 展示上的过度由花费上的过度生长而来。

branches.en: Speech that wanders past measure is the rhetorical sense.
branches.cn: 越过分寸的言辞是修辞义项。

branches.en: Both overspending and a wild claim are departures from the reasonable course.
branches.cn: 花钱过度与荒唐主张都是对合理轨道的偏离。

intro.en: Extravagance is extra plus vagari, and English builds extravagant, extravagantly, and extravaganza on the same base.
intro.cn: extravagance 由 extra 与 vagari 构成，英语在同一基座上造出 extravagant、extravagantly 与 extravaganza。

latinIntro.en: Latin extra means outside, vagari means to wander, and extravagari means to wander out of bounds.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extra 意为在外，vagari 意为游荡，extravagari 意为游荡出界。

items.example: The prefix extra- marks what lies outside.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 extra- 标记处于外部的东西。

items.example: Vagari supplies the wandering image.
items.exampleCN: vagari 提供「游荡」的意象。

items.example: Extravagari joins the two Latin parts.
items.exampleCN: extravagari 把两个拉丁语部分结合起来。

items.example: The suffix -ance turns the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ance 把动词变为名词。

items.example: Extravagance keeps the noun sense.
items.exampleCN: extravagance 保留名词含义。

items.example: The suffix -ant forms the adjective extravagant.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 构成形容词 extravagant。

items.example: Extravagant describes the person or the price.
items.exampleCN: extravagant 可以形容人或价格。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms extravagantly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 extravagantly。

items.example: Extravagantly describes how money is spent.
items.exampleCN: extravagantly 描述花钱的方式。

items.example: Extravaganza came through Italian with the same root.
items.exampleCN: extravaganza 经意大利语传入，词根相同。

latinEntries.example: Extra is the first element of the compound.
latinEntries.exampleCN: extra 是这个复合词的第一部分。

definition_zh: 奢侈的；挥霍的；昂贵的；夸张的
definition_en: spending or costing much more than is necessary, or going beyond what is reasonable
core_image: 一只塞满购物袋却还要再买的手
scene: 朋友劝他别再添置第三块名表，他却说这只是小爱好。His friends urged him to stop buying a third luxury watch, yet he called his extravagant habit a small hobby.
sceneCN: 这里 extravagant 是「奢侈的、挥霍的」（第 1 个义项：花钱远超所需）；句意：朋友劝他别再添置第三块名表，他却说这只是小爱好。

pos.zh: 奢侈的；挥霍的；昂贵的；夸张的

derivatives.zh: 形容词词尾 -ant 换为 -ance 构成的同族名词，义为「奢侈；铺张」
形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「奢侈地；夸张地」
与词根同源的意大利语形式，义为「华丽的娱乐演出」

senses.title: Spending far too much
senses.definition: spending money far beyond what is needed or sensible
senses.definitionCN: 花钱远远超出需要或合理的程度
senses.example: They were criticised for their extravagant way of living.
senses.exampleCN: 他们因奢侈的生活方式受到批评。
senses.why: Extra means outside, and vagari means to wander, so the spending has wandered past the limit.
senses.whyCN: extra 意为在外，vagari 意为游荡，所以这种花费游荡到了限度之外。

senses.title: Costing far too much
senses.definition: costing much more than the thing is worth
senses.definitionCN: 价格远高于其实际价值
senses.example: He bought an extravagant watch that he rarely wears.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了一块很少戴的昂贵手表。
senses.why: A price that goes outside the reasonable range is extravagant in the same literal way.
senses.whyCN: 价格越出合理区间，按同样的字面逻辑也是「奢侈的」。

senses.title: Beyond what is reasonable
senses.definition: going past the limits of what is fair or sensible
senses.definitionCN: 超出公平或合理限度
senses.example: The company made extravagant demands in the negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在谈判中提出了过分的要求。
senses.why: Wandering beyond bounds applies to demands and behaviour as well as to money.
senses.whyCN: 「游荡出界」既能用于钱财，也能用于要求和行为。

senses.title: Showy and exaggerated
senses.definition: expressed in a way that is more dramatic than the facts deserve
senses.definitionCN: 表达得比事实应有的程度更夸张
senses.example: The film won praise for its extravagant visual style.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片因夸张的视觉风格受到称赞。
senses.why: Style that steps outside restraint looks extravagant, which is why the word praises and blames at once.
senses.whyCN: 越过克制的风格显得夸张，所以这个词既能褒也能贬。

senses.title: Wildly imaginative
senses.definition: so unlikely or fanciful that it seems to leave reality behind
senses.definitionCN: 极不可能或异想天开，仿佛脱离了现实
senses.example: The witness told an extravagant story no one believed.
senses.exampleCN: 证人讲了一个没人相信的离奇故事。
senses.why: The oldest image is wandering out of the proper place, and an unbelievable story wanders furthest.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是游荡出应有的位置，而不可信的故事游荡得最远。

intro.en: Extravagant comes from Latin extravagans, the participle of extravagari, to wander out of bounds.
intro.cn: extravagant 来自拉丁语 extravagans，即 extravagari（游荡出界）的分词形式。

items.en: Extra means outside or beyond the limit.
items.cn: extra 意为在外、超出限度。

items.en: Vagari means to wander about without a fixed course.
items.cn: vagari 意为没有固定路线地漫游。

items.en: Extravagari means to roam beyond the proper boundary.
items.cn: extravagari 意为游荡到应有边界之外。

items.en: Stravagante describes a person who behaves wildly.
items.cn: stravagante 形容行为狂放的人。

items.en: Extravagant passes into French as a word for wild conduct.
items.cn: extravagant 传入法语，用来指狂放的行为。

items.en: English borrows extravagant for wild conduct and later for overspending.
items.cn: 英语借入 extravagant 指狂放行为，后来又用于花钱过度。

note.en: Extravagant shares its Latin root with extravagance and extravaganza, and stands near lavish, exorbitant, and excessive.
note.cn: extravagant 与 extravagance、extravaganza 同根，意义上靠近 lavish、exorbitant 与 excessive。

entries.definition: the habit of spending too much
in an excessive manner
a lavish show or spectacle
generous or plentiful to excess
far higher than is reasonable
more than is reasonable or necessary

normalIntro.en: Extravagant carries extra, outside, and vagari, to wander: the word pictures money or style wandering past its proper limit.
normalIntro.cn: extravagant 含有 extra（在外）与 vagari（游荡）：它描绘钱财或风格游荡过了应有的界限。

normal.en: Extra plus vagari gives the idea of wandering outside the proper limit.
normal.cn: extra 加 vagari 给出「游荡到应有界限之外」的意思。

normal.en: An extravagant person spends without counting the cost.
normal.cn: extravagant 的人花钱不计成本。

normal.en: An extravagant gift costs far more than the occasion needs.
normal.cn: extravagant gift 的价格远超场合所需。

normal.en: Extravagant praise is praise that goes beyond the facts.
normal.cn: extravagant praise 是超出事实的赞美。

normal.en: Compare lavish: lavish stresses abundance, extravagant stresses passing the limit.
normal.cn: 对比 lavish：lavish 强调丰盛，extravagant 强调越过限度。

abstract.en: Picture a coin rolling past the edge of a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币滚过桌沿。

abstract.en: Imagine a price tag that keeps rising out of sight.
abstract.cn: 想象一张不断上涨、看不到头的价签。

abstract.en: Think of a speech delivered with far too many grand gestures.
abstract.cn: 想象一场手势夸张得过分的演讲。

examples.en: The wedding was extravagant, with flowers flown in from another country.
examples.cn: 这场婚礼很铺张，鲜花是从国外空运来的。

examples.en: His extravagant claims about the product were easy to disprove.
examples.cn: 他对该产品夸大的说法很容易被驳倒。

examples.en: She has extravagant tastes but a modest income.
examples.cn: 她品味奢华，收入却不高。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「extra + 逛」——读作「额外逛」：逛得越远花得越凶，人既显得奢侈又显得夸张；这只是读音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 extra（在外）+ vagari（游荡）→ 晚期拉丁语 extravagans（游荡出界的）→ 意大利语 stravagante → 法语 extravagant → 英语 extravagant，核心义「越出限度的」。

sensesIntro.en: Extravagant begins with money spent outside need, extends to high prices and unreasonable demands, then to showy style and finally to stories beyond belief.
sensesIntro.cn: extravagant 从花到需要之外的钱开始，延伸到高价与过分的要求，再到浮夸的风格，最后指不可信的故事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin rolling past the edge of the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币滚过桌沿。

branches.en: Overspending is the core money sense of the word.
branches.cn: 花钱过度是这个词核心的金钱义项。

branches.en: A price past the reasonable range is the price sense.
branches.cn: 越出合理区间的价格是它的价格义项。

branches.en: Demands beyond fairness extend the image to behaviour.
branches.cn: 超出公平的要求把这一意象延伸到行为。

branches.en: Showy style is the aesthetic sense of passing the limit.
branches.cn: 浮夸风格是「越过限度」在审美上的义项。

branches.en: Both a wasteful buyer and a wild story have left the proper track.
branches.cn: 挥霍的买家与离奇的故事都离开了应有的轨道。

intro.en: Extravagant is extra plus vagari with the ending -ant, and its English family runs through -ance, -ly, and the Italian noun extravaganza.
intro.cn: extravagant 由 extra 与 vagari 加词尾 -ant 构成，英语词族经 -ance、-ly 以及意大利语名词 extravaganza 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin extra means outside, vagari means to wander, and the participle extravagans means wandering out of bounds.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extra 意为在外，vagari 意为游荡，分词 extravagans 意为游荡出界。

items.example: The prefix extra- puts the action outside a limit.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 extra- 把动作置于限度之外。

items.example: Vagari gives the image of roaming without a course.
items.exampleCN: vagari 给出无路线漫游的意象。

items.example: Extravagans is the participle behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: extravagans 是这个形容词背后的分词形式。

items.example: The ending -ant forms an adjective from a verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 从动词词干构成形容词。

items.example: Extravagant keeps the sense of passing the limit.
items.exampleCN: extravagant 保留「越过限度」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ance forms the noun extravagance.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ance 构成名词 extravagance。

items.example: Extravagance names the habit itself.
items.exampleCN: extravagance 指这种习惯本身。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb extravagantly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 extravagantly。

items.example: Extravagantly describes the manner of spending.
items.exampleCN: extravagantly 描述花钱的方式。

items.example: Extravaganza entered English through Italian.
items.exampleCN: extravaganza 经意大利语进入英语。

latinEntries.example: Extra marks position outside a boundary.
latinEntries.exampleCN: extra 标记边界之外的位置。

latinEntries.example: Extravagans is the direct Latin source.
latinEntries.exampleCN: extravagans 是直接的拉丁语来源。

core_image: 温度计的水银柱冲到最顶端
scene: 该地区正经历极端天气。The region is experiencing extreme weather.
sceneCN: 这里 extreme 是「极度的、极端的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：该地区正经历极端天气。

derivatives.zh: 极其；非常
末端；极端

senses.title: Very great in degree
senses.definition: very great in degree or intensity
senses.definitionCN: 程度或强度非常大的
senses.example: The desert reaches extreme temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 沙漠会达到极端温度。
senses.why: The core sense is the farthest point of a scale.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是刻度上最远的一点。

senses.title: Far from moderate
senses.definition: far from what is usual, moderate, or acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 远离通常、温和或可接受范围的
senses.example: The group holds extreme views.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团体持有极端观点。

senses.whyCN: 刻度的远端变成政治判断。

senses.title: The furthest point
senses.definition: the furthest or most severe point of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物最远或最严重的点
senses.example: The two extremes rarely meet.
senses.exampleCN: 两个极端很少相遇。
senses.why: The adjective becomes the endpoint itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词变成端点本身。

intro.en: Extreme comes from Latin extremus, the superlative of exterus, outward.
intro.cn: extreme 来自拉丁语 extremus，是 exterus（向外的）的最高级。

items.en: Exterus means outward.
items.cn: exterus 意为向外的。

items.en: Extremus means farthest out.
items.cn: extremus 意为最靠外的。

items.en: Extreme passes through French into English.
items.cn: extreme 经法语进入英语。

items.en: Extreme describes the far end of a scale.
items.cn: extreme 描述刻度的最远端。

items.en: Extreme also describes severe weather and views.
items.cn: 现代英语中 extreme 也形容极端天气与观点。

note.en: Extreme is the far end; extra is an addition.
note.cn: extreme 是最远端，extra 则是额外添加。

entries.definition: to remove or take out
a person with special knowledge
to pass waste out of the body
very bad or intense
very strong or extreme
far beyond the usual

normalIntro.en: Extreme points to the farthest end of any scale.
normalIntro.cn: extreme 指向任何刻度的最远端。

normal.en: The region suffers extreme heat in summer.
normal.cn: 这个地区夏天酷热难耐。

normal.en: They took extreme measures to stop the fire.
normal.cn: 他们采取极端措施阻止大火。

normal.en: The family lives in extreme poverty.
normal.cn: 这家人生活在极度贫困中。

normal.en: Do not go to extremes in dieting.
normal.cn: 节食不要走极端。

normal.en: At the other extreme, the lake is frozen.
normal.cn: 在另一个极端，湖面结着冰。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer pushed to its highest mark.
abstract.cn: 想象温度计的水银冲到最高点。

abstract.en: Imagine a road ending at a cliff edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路终止在悬崖边。

abstract.en: Think of a scale with weights at both ends.
abstract.cn: 想象天平两端都压着砝码。

examples.en: The mountain is dangerous in extreme weather.
examples.cn: 在极端天气下，这座山很危险。

examples.en: Their views are too extreme for most voters.
examples.cn: 他们的观点对多数选民来说太极端。

examples.en: The temperature swung from one extreme to the other.
examples.cn: 温度从一个极端摆到另一个极端。

dict_mnemonic.text: extreme 与 extra 同源：extra 是「超出」，extreme 是「超出到最远端」，即极端。

root: 源自拉丁语 extremus（最靠外的），是 exterus（向外的）的最高级，核心义「刻度或范围的最远端」。

sensesIntro.en: Extreme means very great in degree, far from moderate, or the furthest point.
sensesIntro.cn: extreme 意为程度极大、远离温和，或最远的端点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gauge needle at the red end.

branches.en: The base sense is the far end of a scale.
branches.cn: 基础义是刻度的最远端。

branches.en: The far end becomes a judgment of views.
branches.cn: 最远端变成对观点的评判。

branches.en: The adjective becomes the endpoint itself.
branches.cn: 形容词变成端点本身。

branches.en: Great degree and immoderate views both sit at the edge.
branches.cn: 极大程度与偏激观点都位于边缘。

branches.en: Extreme views and extreme situations share the same edge.
branches.cn: 极端观点与极端处境共享同一条边缘。

intro.en: Extreme comes from the Latin exterus family and has a large modern word family.
intro.cn: extreme 来自拉丁语 exterus 词族，现代词族很大。

latinIntro.en: Latin extremus and exterus are the source forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extremus 与 exterus 是来源形式。

items.example: The task is extremely difficult.

definition_zh: 向外的；有外转倾向的；注意力向外的；向外表达的
definition_en: directed or tending outward, used chiefly in technical writing for an outward direction, outward-directed attention, or feeling that moves outward toward other people
core_image: 一根枝条从植株中心向外弯出去，尖端朝着外面的世界
scene: 心理学的旧文献里，作者把注意力朝向外部世界的那种倾向称为外倾的。Older psychology texts described that outward-turning tendency as extroversive.
sceneCN: 这里 extroversive 是「有外转倾向的、外倾的」（第 1 个义项：方向朝外、带有向外转的倾向）；句意：较早的心理学文献把这种向外转的倾向称为 extroversive。

pos.zh: 向外的；有外转倾向的；注意力向外的；向外表达的

derivatives.zh: extroversive + -ly，义为「向外地；以外倾的方式」
extroversive + -ness，义为「外倾性；向外转的性质」
extrovert + -sion，义为「外向性；外倾」，与本词共享「向外转」的词干

senses.title: Tending outward in direction
senses.definition: of a movement, structure, or direction: turned or tending toward the outside
senses.definitionCN: 指运动、结构或方向：朝外转或倾向于朝外
senses.example: The shell shows an extroversive curve along its outer edge.
senses.exampleCN: 贝壳沿外缘呈现出一道向外的弧线。
senses.why: Extro- is the Latin extra, outside, and the ending comes from versus, the turned participle of vertere, so the word names a direction of turning rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: extro- 来自拉丁语 extra（外面），词尾来自 vertere 的分词 versus（转），所以这个词命名的是「转的方向」，而不是某个人。

senses.title: Directing attention outward
senses.definition: in technical psychology: directing interest and attention toward objects and people outside the self
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学专业用法中：把兴趣与注意力指向自我之外的事物和人
senses.example: The older literature set the extroversive attitude against the introversive one.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的文献把外倾的态度与内倾的态度对立起来。
senses.why: The direction named in sense one is applied to the mind: attention that turns outward becomes an attitude, not just a line on a diagram.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项里的方向被用到心智上：向外转的注意力成了一种态度，而不只是图上的一条线。

senses.title: Expressed outward
senses.definition: of feeling or energy: tending to be expressed outward toward other people rather than held inside
senses.definitionCN: 指感情或精力：倾向于向外朝别人表达，而不是憋在心里
senses.example: Her extroversive warmth made the new students feel included.
senses.exampleCN: 她那种向外流露的热情让新来的学生觉得自己被接纳。
senses.why: A feeling that tends outward crosses the boundary of the self, so the rare adjective can describe warmth and energy as well as direction.
senses.whyCN: 倾向于朝外的感情会越过自我的边界，所以这个少见的形容词既能写方向，也能写热情与精力。

intro.en: Extroversive is generally explained as an English adjective built on Latin material: extra, outside, plus versus, the turned participle of vertere, plus the suffix -ive. It appears mainly in technical psychology, as the counterpart of introversive.
intro.cn: 一般认为 extroversive 是用拉丁语材料在英语里构成的形容词：extra（外面）加 vertere 的分词 versus（转），再加词尾 -ive。它主要出现在心理学专业写作中，是 introversive 的对应词。

items.en: Extra means outside, beyond, or past the boundary of something.
items.cn: extra 意为在外、超出，或越过某物的边界。

items.en: Vertere means to turn, and its participle versus means turned or facing.
items.cn: vertere 意为转，它的分词 versus 意为「转了的、朝向的」。

items.en: The adjective suffix -ivus marks a tendency or a quality, the source of English -ive.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词词尾 -ivus 表示倾向或性质，是英语 -ive 的来源。

items.en: Technical writing builds extroversive on that Latin pattern, pairing it with introversive as its opposite.
items.cn: 技术写作按那个拉丁语模式造出 extroversive，并与作为反义词的 introversive 配对使用。

items.en: The term is used for attention and attitudes that turn toward the outer world rather than the inner life.
items.cn: 这个词用来指朝向外部世界、而非内心生活的注意力与态度。

items.en: The adjective stays rare and technical, while extroverted carries the everyday sense of outgoing.
items.cn: 这个形容词始终少见且偏技术，日常表示「外向」则由 extroverted 承担。

note.en: The first group holds the extrovert word family and the matching introversive opposite; the second group holds words for the outward direction, sociability, and open expression that the adjective can imply.
note.cn: 第一组是 extrovert 的同族词与对应的 introversive 反义词；第二组是这个词可能蕴含的「朝外、爱交际、外露」三类近义词。

normal.en: Extro- is Latin extra, outside, and -versive comes from versus, turned: the word means turned outward.

normal.en: The suffix -ive signals a tendency, so extroversive means tending to turn outward, not turned outward for good.

normal.en: Introversive is its mirror image, built with intro-, within.

normal.en: The word usually keeps company with tendency, orientation, attention, or type.

sensesIntro.en: Extroversive is the rare technical adjective of the outward turn: it first names a direction, then an attitude of attention, then a tendency of feeling to move outward. It describes a bearing or tendency, while extroverted describes a person or manner already turned outward.
sensesIntro.cn: extroversive 是表示「向外转」的少见技术性形容词：先命名方向，再指注意力的态度，最后指感情向外流动的倾向。它描写的是方向或倾向，而 extroverted 描写已经朝外的人或举止。

branches.cn: 一道弧线与一个热情的手势，是同一种向外转在两种尺度上的样子。

intro.en: Extroversive joins the Latin prefix extra-, outside, to versus, the turned participle of vertere, to turn, and closes with the adjective suffix -ive. Its family includes extrovert, extroverted, extroversion, and introversive.

latinIntro.en: Latin extra means outside, vertere means to turn, and versus means turned; English used those pieces to make an adjective of outward tendency.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extra 意为在外，vertere 意为转，versus 意为「转了的」；英语用这些材料造出一个表示向外倾向的形容词。

definition_en: a person who is outgoing, enjoys the company of other people, and turns attention outward rather than inward

senses.title: A person turned toward other people
senses.definition: a person who is lively, talks easily, and enjoys being with other people
senses.definitionCN: 活泼、容易开口，并且喜欢和别人待在一起的人
senses.example: The new manager is an extrovert who knows everyone by the end of the first week.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的经理是个外向的人，第一周结束时就认识了所有人。
senses.why: Latin extra means outside and vertere means to turn, so an extrovert is literally a person turned outward toward the world of people.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 extra 意为「外面」，vertere 意为「转」；extrovert 字面上就是「朝外转的人」，把注意力转向有人的外部世界。

senses.title: The psychological type
senses.definition: in psychology, a person whose attention is directed outward and who gains energy from people and activity, as opposed to an introvert
senses.definitionCN: 心理学上指注意力朝外、从人群和活动中获得精力的人，与内向者相对
senses.example: Jung described the extrovert as someone whose interest flows out toward objects and people.
senses.exampleCN: 荣格把外倾者描述为一个兴趣向外流向事物与人的人。
senses.why: The word was coined as a technical label, so the outward turn became a measurable personality type with a name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是作为心理学术语被造出来的，于是「向外转」变成了一种有名称、可描述的人格类型。

senses.title: The attention-loving performer
senses.titleCN: 爱出风头的人；场上的活跃分子
senses.definition: a person who enjoys being the centre of attention in a group and performs for other people
senses.definitionCN: 喜欢成为一群人注意力的中心、乐于在别人面前表演的人
senses.example: Every party needs an extrovert to get the dancing started.
senses.exampleCN: 每个聚会都需要一个爱出风头的人来带动大家跳起舞。
senses.why: A person turned outward also turns toward an audience, so the taste for company grows into a taste for the spotlight.
senses.whyCN: 一个朝外转的人也会转向观众；喜欢有人作伴，便慢慢长成喜欢站在聚光灯下。

senses.title: The outward side of a personality
senses.definition: the part of a personality that turns outward and enjoys company, sometimes imagined as a separate self
senses.definitionCN: 性格中朝外、喜欢与人相处的那一面，有时被想象成一个单独的自我
senses.example: Quiet for most of the week, he lets the extrovert out on Saturday nights.
senses.exampleCN: 他一周里大多时候很安静，到了周六晚上就把心里那个外向的自己放出来。
senses.why: The same outward turn can be imagined as one side of a person, so even a shy person can speak of the extrovert inside.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「向外转」可以被想象成一个人性格中的一面，所以连害羞的人也能说自己心里住着一个 extrovert。

intro.en: Extrovert is a made-up Latin compound: extra, outside, plus vertere, to turn, so it names a person turned outward. It entered English in the early twentieth century as a psychological label, probably by way of German.
intro.cn: extrovert 是一个用拉丁语材料造出的复合词：extra（外面）加 vertere（转），字面就是「朝外转的人」。它在大约二十世纪初作为心理学术语进入英语，一般认为经由德语传入。

items.en: Extra means outside, beyond, or past the boundary of something.
items.cn: extra 意为在外、超出，或越过某物的边界。

items.en: Vertere means to turn, and it is the verb behind convert, divert, invert, and reverse.
items.cn: vertere 意为转，是 convert、divert、invert、reverse 共同的动词词根。

items.en: The two elements were put together in modern times to name a turning outward; no classical Latin author used the combination as an everyday verb.
items.cn: 人们把这两个成分在近代拼在一起，用来命名「朝外转」；古典拉丁作家并未把这个组合当作日常动词使用。

items.en: The psychologist Carl Jung wrote of the extravertierte personality, the type whose interest turns outward toward the world.
items.cn: 心理学家荣格写到 extravertierte 人格，即兴趣朝外转向世界的那种类型。

items.en: English took the idea up as extrovert; the o spelling, probably shaped by introvert, became the standard form.
items.cn: 英语把这个概念借入为 extrovert；拼写中的 o 一般认为受 introvert 影响，后来成为标准形式。

items.en: The clinical label widened into everyday use for any sociable, outgoing person, and later for the outward side of a personality.
items.cn: 这个临床标签扩大为日常用语，指任何爱交际、外向的人，后来又指性格中外向的一面。

note.en: The first group holds the extrovert word family and its opposite pattern; the second group holds everyday words for sociable people.
note.cn: 第一组是 extrovert 的同族词与相反构词；第二组是日常用来形容爱交际者的近义词。

normal.cn: a natural extrovert 指天生就爱与人相处的人。

normal.en: To come across as an extrovert means you seem outgoing even if you are not.

abstract.en: Picture a lamp fixed to a chest, its beam sweeping the crowded room.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯装在胸口，光束扫过满屋的人。

abstract.cn: 想象一束聚光灯跟着一位客人从一桌走到另一桌。

examples.cn: 她小时候天生外向，每条街都能交到朋友。

examples.cn: 课程把每个外向的学员和一个更安静的搭档配成一组做任务。

examples.en: Extroverts often find open-plan offices easier than quiet introverts do.
examples.cn: 外向的人往往比安静内向的人更能适应开放式办公室。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person whose face and attention are turned outward, toward the room.

branches.en: The everyday sense is simply the person who turns toward other people.

branches.en: Psychology turns that posture into a named personality type.
branches.cn: 心理学把这种姿态变成一种有名称的人格类型。

branches.en: The outward turn also faces an audience, so the type becomes the performer.
branches.cn: 朝外转也意味着面向观众，于是这种类型成了台上的活跃分子。

branches.en: The same outward turn can be a whole person or one side of a personality.

branches.en: The trait and the spotlight share one engine: energy drawn from being seen and heard.

senses.title: Outgoing and sociable

senses.title: Of the extraverted type
