senses.why: Psychology took the noun and added -ed to make a trait adjective, so the outward turn became a measurable quality of a person.
senses.whyCN: 心理学取来名词加上 -ed，造出描述特质的形容词，于是「朝外转」变成一种可以测量的人格性质。

senses.title: Shown openly
senses.definition: of feelings, gestures, or style: expressed openly so that other people can see them
senses.definitionCN: 指感情、动作或风格：公开表露出来，让别人看得见
senses.example: Their extroverted display of affection embarrassed the quieter guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他们那种外露的亲昵举动让较安静的客人有些尴尬。
senses.why: Feelings turned outward do not stay inside; the same direction that shapes character also shapes visible expression.
senses.whyCN: 朝外的感情不会留在心里；塑造性格的那同一个方向，也塑造看得见的表达。

senses.title: Outward-looking
senses.definition: interested in the world and people outside the self rather than in one own inner life
senses.definitionCN: 对外部世界和他人感兴趣，而不是只关注自己的内心
senses.example: Her extroverted curiosity about other cultures took her abroad for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 她那种对外部世界的好奇让她出国待了一年。
senses.why: The core turn is toward what lies outside, so attention itself can be called extroverted even without a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 核心的「转」朝向外部，所以即使没有人群，注意力本身也可以被称为 extroverted。

intro.en: Extroverted is the adjective built from extrovert with -ed, and it carries the same Latin extra, outside, and vertere, to turn. It entered English with the psychological vocabulary of the early twentieth century.
intro.cn: extroverted 是由 extrovert 加 -ed 构成的形容词，同样带着拉丁语 extra（外面）与 vertere（转）。它随二十世纪初的心理学词汇进入英语。

items.en: Extra means outside, beyond, or past the boundary of something.
items.cn: extra 意为在外、超出，或越过某物的边界。

items.en: Vertere means to turn, and it is the verb behind convert, divert, invert, and reverse.
items.cn: vertere 意为转，是 convert、divert、invert、reverse 共同的动词词根。

items.en: The noun extrovert arrives as a psychological label, and the adjective extroverted follows with the participial ending -ed.
items.cn: 名词 extrovert 作为心理学术语进入英语，形容词 extroverted 随后带着分词词尾 -ed 出现。

items.en: The -ed form spreads from clinical writing into descriptions of lively, sociable people.
items.cn: 这个带 -ed 的形式从临床写作扩散到对活泼、爱交际者的描写。

items.en: Modern dictionaries also record the shorter form extrovert as an adjective, especially in British use.
items.cn: 现代词典也收录了更短的形式 extrovert 作形容词，尤其在英式英语中。

note.en: The first group holds the extrovert word family and its opposite pattern; the second group holds adjectives close to the sociable and expressive sides of the word.
note.cn: 第一组是 extrovert 的同族词与相反构词；第二组是与「爱交际、外露」这两面相近的形容词。

entries.definition: an outgoing person
entries.definitionCN: 外向的人（本形容词所由来的名词）

entries.definition: the quality of being outgoing
turned inward and quiet
entries.definitionCN: 内向的；安静的（由 intro-「向内」构成，与本词方向相反）

entries.definition: friendly and eager to meet people
fond of being with other people
willing to show affection or feelings openly

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -ed ending, the word family, and the phrases extroverted actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子利用 -ed 词尾、同族词，以及 extroverted 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The -ed ending means the turn is complete: the person has been turned outward.
normal.cn: -ed 词尾表示这个「转」已经完成：人已经被转向外面。

normal.en: The family runs extrovert, extroversion, extroverted, with introverted as the mirror image.
normal.cn: 词族包括 extrovert、extroversion、extroverted，而 introverted 是它的镜像反义。

normal.en: An extroverted personality is the standard phrase for the trait.
normal.cn: an extroverted personality 是描述这种特质的常用说法。

normal.en: Because it is a long adjective, the comparative is more extroverted, not extroverter.
normal.cn: 因为这是多音节形容词，比较级用 more extroverted，而不是 extroverter。

normal.en: Outgoing is warmer and more everyday; extroverted is more technical and stresses direction.
normal.cn: outgoing 更亲切、更日常；extroverted 更偏术语，强调方向。

abstract.en: Picture a window pushed open and the whole room turning toward the street.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇窗被推开，整个房间都转向街道。

abstract.en: Think of a gauge whose needle sits permanently in the outward half.
abstract.cn: 想象一个仪表，指针永远停在外侧那一半。

abstract.en: See feelings written on a face instead of kept behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象感情写在脸上，而不是藏在脸后面。

examples.en: She became more extroverted after a year in the drama club.
examples.cn: 在戏剧社待了一年之后，她变得外向了。

examples.en: His extroverted greeting put the nervous visitors at ease.
examples.cn: 他外向的招呼让紧张的来访者放松下来。

examples.en: Extroverted children may find it harder to work quietly alone.
examples.cn: 外向的孩子可能更难安静地独自做事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱克戳沃提德」——前半听成「爱往外戳」，后面再拖一个 -ed：一个已经被转朝外的人；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 extra（在外）+ vertere（转）→ extrovert（朝外转的人）+ 形容词词尾 -ed → extroverted；核心义「已经朝外转的」。

sensesIntro.en: Extroverted keeps the outward turn of extrovert but applies it to manner, to the measured trait, to visible feeling, and finally to attention itself.
sensesIntro.cn: extroverted 保留 extrovert 的「朝外转」，但把它用到举止、可测量的特质、看得见的感情，最后用到注意力本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a window pushed open, with the whole person turned toward the street.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇窗被推开，整个人都转向街道。

branches.en: The everyday sense is the settled sociable manner.
branches.cn: 日常义项是已经定型的爱交际举止。

branches.en: The trait sense measures that manner as a personality dimension.
branches.cn: 特质义项把这种举止当作人格维度来测量。

branches.en: The same turn outward makes feeling visible on the surface.
branches.cn: 同一种朝外转，让感情显露在表面上。

branches.en: With no crowd at all, the turn becomes pure outward attention.
branches.cn: 即使没有人群，这种转也变成纯粹的对外注意。

branches.en: Manner, expression, and curiosity are one outward turn at three depths.
branches.cn: 举止、表达与好奇，是同一种朝外转在三个深度上的样子。

intro.en: Extroverted is extrovert plus -ed, built on Latin extra, outside, and vertere, to turn. The family includes extroversion, introverted, convert, and divert.
intro.cn: extroverted 是 extrovert 加 -ed，建立在拉丁语 extra（在外）与 vertere（转）之上；同族词包括 extroversion、introverted、convert 与 divert。

latinIntro.en: Latin extra means outside and vertere means to turn; English added the participial ending -ed to the noun to make the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extra 意为在外，vertere 意为转；英语给名词加上分词词尾 -ed，构成这个形容词。

items.example: The prefix points the motion away from the self.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向自我之外。

items.example: Vertere is the turning verb at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: vertere 是这个词核心的「转」动词。

items.example: Convert and divert both end in the same turning element.
items.exampleCN: convert 与 divert 都以同一个表示「转」的成分结尾。

items.meaningCN: 表示「已处于某种状态」的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix turns the noun into a description of a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成对一个人的描述。

items.example: Extrovert is the base noun of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: extrovert 是这个形容词所由来的名词。

items.example: Extroverted describes the settled outward manner.
items.exampleCN: extroverted 描写已经定型的朝外举止。

items.example: Extroversion names the trait in abstract form.
items.exampleCN: extroversion 以抽象形式命名这种特质。

items.example: Introverted reverses the prefix: inward instead of outward.
items.exampleCN: introverted 把前缀反过来：向内而非向外。

items.example: Convert adds con-, together, to the turning root.
items.exampleCN: convert 在「转」词根前加了 con-（一起）。

items.example: Divert turns something away from its path.
items.exampleCN: divert 把某物从原路上转开。

definition_zh: 挤出；挤压成形；挤出物；喷出
definition_en: the act of forcing something out, the shaping of material by pushing it through a shaped opening, the product so formed, and in geology the pouring out of lava onto the surface
core_image: 软泥被从带孔的模具里推出来，变成一条长长的条状物
scene: 工厂把加热的铝坯放进压机，从模具的小孔里挤出一条长长的型材。The extrusion happens as the heated aluminium is forced through the die.
sceneCN: 这里 extrusion 是「挤压成形」（第 2 个义项：把材料从模具孔里挤出来成形）；句意：加热的铝被强行挤过模具，这个过程就叫 extrusion。

pos.zh: 挤出；挤压成形；挤出物；喷出

derivatives.zh: extrusion 的动词形式，由 ex-（出）加 trudere（推）构成，义为「挤出；挤压成形」
extrude + -er，义为「挤出机；挤压机」
extrusion + -ive，义为「喷出的；挤出的」，尤指喷出岩

senses.title: The act of forcing out
senses.definition: the act of pushing or forcing something out of a container, opening, or body
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从容器、开口或物体内部推出来、挤出来的动作
senses.example: The extrusion of paste from the tube was slow and uneven.
senses.exampleCN: 把膏体从管里挤出来的过程又慢又不均匀。
senses.why: Ex- means out and trudere means to thrust, so the noun starts as the bare act of thrusting something out.
senses.whyCN: ex- 意为「出」，trudere 意为「推」，所以这个名词最初就是「把某物推出去」的动作本身。

senses.title: Shaping through a die
senses.definition: a manufacturing process in which heated metal, plastic, or food is forced through a shaped opening called a die
senses.definitionCN: 把加热的金属、塑料或食物强行挤过称为模具的定型开口，从而成形的制造工艺
senses.example: Aluminium extrusion gives long profiles for window frames.
senses.exampleCN: 铝挤压为窗框生产出长长的型材。
senses.why: Industry turned the general push into a precise craft: the opening decides the shape, so thrusting out becomes forming.
senses.whyCN: 工业把一般的「推出去」变成精确的工艺：出口决定形状，于是「挤出」变成了「成形」。

senses.title: The extruded product
senses.definition: a piece or mass of material produced by being forced through a die
senses.definitionCN: 被强行挤过模具而生产出来的一块或一团材料
senses.example: Workers stack the finished extrusions on racks to cool.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把成型的挤压制品堆在架子上冷却。
senses.why: Once the process has a name, the thing that comes out can take the same name, a common shift from action to product.
senses.whyCN: 过程有了名称之后，从模具里出来的东西也用同一个词来称呼，这是从「动作」到「产物」的常见转义。

senses.title: Geological outpouring
senses.definition: in geology, the pushing of magma or lava out onto the earth surface, or the rock formed this way
senses.definitionCN: 地质学上指岩浆或熔岩被推到地表，或由此形成的岩石
senses.example: Volcanic extrusion built the ridge in a series of flows.
senses.exampleCN: 火山喷出物在一系列熔岩流中堆出了这道山脊。
senses.why: The same thrusting out describes molten rock forced to the surface, so the industrial word also names a geological event.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「向外推」也能描述熔岩被推到地表，于是工业用语也用来命名地质事件。

intro.en: Extrusion is generally traced to Latin extrudere, to thrust out, from ex-, out, and trudere, to thrust. The noun extrusio then passes into English, where it gains industrial and geological senses.
intro.cn: 一般认为 extrusion 可追溯到拉丁语 extrudere（推出），由 ex-（出）与 trudere（推）构成；名词 extrusio 随后进入英语，并发展出工业与地质义项。

items.en: Ex- means out of or away from, the same prefix seen in exit and export.
items.cn: ex- 意为「出、离开」，与 exit、export 里的前缀相同。

items.en: Trudere means to thrust or push, and it is the verb behind intrude and protrude.
items.cn: trudere 意为推、挤，是 intrude 与 protrude 背后的动词。

items.en: Extrudere joins the two pieces and means to thrust out or drive out.
items.cn: extrudere 把这两个成分合起来，意为「推出、逐出」。

items.en: The noun extrusio names a thrusting out, and English takes it up as extrusion.
items.cn: 名词 extrusio 表示「推出」，英语把它借入为 extrusion。

items.en: Extrusion first names the simple action of forcing something out.
items.cn: extrusion 最初只指把某物强行挤出的简单动作。

items.en: Industry adds the shaping of metal and plastic through a die, and geology adds lava forced onto the surface.
items.cn: 工业用法增加了用模具使金属与塑料成形的意思，地质用法增加了熔岩被推到地表的意思。

note.en: The first group holds the extrusion word family; the second group holds nouns for pushing, throwing, or driving something out.
note.cn: 第一组是 extrusion 的同族词；第二组是表示「推出、抛出、排出」的名词。

entries.definition: to thrust or force something out
entries.definitionCN: 挤出；推出（本名词所由来的动词）

entries.definition: a machine that forces material through a die
formed by being pushed out, especially of rock
entries.definitionCN: 喷出的；挤出的（尤指喷出岩）

entries.definition: the act of forcing something or someone out
something that sticks out, or the act of pushing forward
the act of throwing or forcing something out

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin pieces, the word family with extrude and extruder, and the industrial and geological phrases the noun appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子利用真实的拉丁成分、含 extrude 与 extruder 的同族词，以及这个名词实际出现的工业与地质搭配。

normal.en: Ex- is out and trudere is to thrust, so extrusion is a thrusting out.
normal.cn: ex- 是「出」，trudere 是「推」，所以 extrusion 就是「往外推出去」。

normal.en: Plastic extrusion forces melted plastic through a die, and the die decides the shape.
normal.cn: 塑料挤出把熔化的塑料强行挤过模具，形状由模具决定。

normal.en: The machine is an extruder, the process is extrusion, and the product is also an extrusion.
normal.cn: 机器叫 extruder，过程叫 extrusion，挤出来的产品也叫 extrusion。

normal.en: Extrusive rock is rock that was pushed out onto the surface as lava.
normal.cn: extrusive rock 指熔岩被推到地表后形成的岩石。

normal.en: Compare intrude and protrude: all three carry the pushing root trudere.
normal.cn: 对比 intrude 与 protrude：三者都带着表示「推」的词根 trudere。

abstract.en: Picture toothpaste being squeezed out of a tube onto a brush.
abstract.cn: 想象牙膏被从管里挤到牙刷上。

abstract.en: Picture soft clay pushed through a shaped hole and coming out as a long ribbon.
abstract.cn: 想象软泥被挤过定型的孔，出来时变成一条长带。

abstract.en: Picture a long plastic profile cooling on a rack, still warm from the die.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长长的塑料型材在架子上冷却，还带着模具的余温。

examples.en: The extrusion of tomato paste from the tube was slow.
examples.cn: 番茄膏从管里挤出来的过程很慢。

examples.en: Aluminium extrusion produces long profiles for window frames.
examples.cn: 铝挤压为窗框生产出长长的型材。

examples.en: Each extrusion is checked for shape before it leaves the factory.
examples.cn: 每一件挤压制品出厂前都要检查形状。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex 出，trud 推」——把材料往外推过模具，就是挤压成形；这只是拆词联想，不是词源考证。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（出）+ trudere（推）→ extrudere（推出）→ 名词 extrusio → 英语 extrusion；核心义「把东西往外推出来」，再引申为挤压成形、挤出物与地质喷出。

sensesIntro.en: Extrusion begins as the plain act of thrusting something out, becomes the industrial craft of shaping material through a die, then names the product, and finally describes lava forced onto the surface.
sensesIntro.cn: extrusion 起初只是「把东西推出去」的动作，后来成为用模具使材料成形的工业工艺，再指挤出来的产品，最后指熔岩被推到地表的喷出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft clay pushed through a hole and coming out as a long ribbon.
core.cn: 核心意象：软泥被从孔里推出来，变成一条长长的带状物。

branches.en: The basic sense is the bare act of forcing something out.
branches.cn: 基础义项就是「把东西强行挤出来」的动作。

branches.en: Manufacturing makes that push a shaping craft.
branches.cn: 制造业把这种推挤变成一门成形工艺。

branches.en: The product takes the name of the process that made it.
branches.cn: 产品沿用了制造它的那个过程的名称。

branches.en: Geology applies the same thrust to molten rock reaching the surface.
branches.cn: 地质学把同样的「推」用到抵达地表的熔岩上。

branches.en: Any act of forcing out can end in a piece of material so formed.
branches.cn: 任何「挤出」动作都可能留下由此成形的一块材料。

intro.en: Extrusion is ex-, out, plus trudere, to thrust, with the noun suffix -sion. The same pushing root appears in extrude, extruder, extrusive, intrude, and protrude.
intro.cn: extrusion 由 ex-（出）加 trudere（推），再加名词词尾 -sion 构成；同一个「推」词根也出现在 extrude、extruder、extrusive、intrude 与 protrude 里。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex- means out, trudere means to thrust, and the compound extrudere means to thrust out; extrusio is the noun built on the supine stem extrus-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ex- 意为出，trudere 意为推，复合词 extrudere 意为推出；extrusio 是在动名词干 extrus- 基础上构成的名词。

items.example: The prefix points the motion outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向外面。

items.example: Trudere is the pushing verb at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: trudere 是这个词核心的「推」动词。

items.example: Intrude and protrude both end in the pushing element.
items.exampleCN: intrude 与 protrude 都以这个表示「推」的成分结尾。

items.example: Extrude is the verb that names the action.
items.exampleCN: extrude 是命名这一动作的动词。

items.meaning: the act or product of thrusting out
items.example: Extrusion keeps both the action and the product sense.
items.exampleCN: extrusion 同时保留动作与产物两个义项。

items.example: The extruder pushes the melted material through the die.
items.exampleCN: 挤出机把熔化的材料推过模具。

items.example: Extrusive describes rock that reached the surface.
items.exampleCN: extrusive 描述抵达地表的岩石。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成表示动作的名词。

items.example: Intrude adds in- to the same pushing root.
items.exampleCN: intrude 在同一个「推」词根前加了 in-。

items.meaning: to thrust forward or stick out
items.example: Protrude adds pro-, forward, to the pushing root.
items.exampleCN: protrude 在「推」词根前加了 pro-（向前）。

definition_zh: 热情洋溢的；精力充沛的；茂盛的；丰富的
definition_en: full of lively energy and excitement, or growing thick and abundant
core_image: 春天的枝条疯长，花和叶子多到挤出边界
scene: 球赛结束后，年轻人围着球员又跳又叫，笑声停不下来。The young fans were still exuberant long after the final whistle.
sceneCN: 这里 exuberant 是「热情洋溢的」（第 1 个义项：情绪高涨、活力外露）；句意：终场哨响很久之后，年轻球迷依然热情不减。

pos.zh: 热情洋溢的；精力充沛的；茂盛的；丰富的

derivatives.zh: 由 exuberant 换后缀 -ance 构成的名词，义为「热情；茂盛；丰富」
由 exuberant 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「热情洋溢地」
由 exuberant 加前缀 over- 构成，义为「过分热情的」

senses.title: Full of high spirits
senses.titleCN: 热情洋溢的；兴高采烈的
senses.definition: showing or feeling a lot of lively happiness and excitement
senses.definitionCN: 表现出或感到大量活泼的快乐与兴奋
senses.example: The children were exuberant on the last day of school.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在学期最后一天兴奋极了。
senses.why: Latin uber means fertile abundance, so the word pictures a feeling that overflows.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 uber 意为丰饶多产，所以这个词画的是「满到溢出来」的情绪。

senses.title: Energetic in action or style
senses.titleCN: 精力充沛的；蓬勃有力的
senses.definition: done or performed with vigorous, unrestrained energy
senses.definitionCN: 以旺盛而不受拘束的精力做出或表演
senses.example: Her exuberant dance style filled the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 她蓬勃有力的舞姿充满了整个舞台。
senses.why: The overflow of growth turns into an overflow of movement and performance.
senses.whyCN: 生长上的「溢出」，转成了动作与表演上的「溢出」。

senses.title: Growing thickly
senses.definition: growing vigorously with dense leaves, branches, or flowers
senses.definitionCN: 枝叶或花朵浓密而旺盛地生长
senses.example: Exuberant vines covered the old wall.
senses.exampleCN: 茂盛的藤蔓爬满了那面旧墙。
senses.why: The oldest sense is literal: plants pour out leaves as if from a full udder.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是字面的：植物像从饱满的乳房里涌出一样长出叶子。

senses.title: Rich and abundant
senses.definition: existing in large amounts, especially of imagination or creativity
senses.definitionCN: 大量存在，尤指想象力或创造力
senses.example: The film is full of exuberant colour and invention.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片充满丰富的色彩和创意。
senses.why: Abundance moves from plants to qualities that seem to spill over.
senses.whyCN: 「丰盛」从植物转到那些仿佛会漫出来的品质。

senses.title: Overly ornate
senses.definition: decorated or written in a style that is richer than necessary
senses.definitionCN: 以超过必要程度的华丽风格装饰或书写
senses.example: The baroque church is famous for its exuberant carvings.
senses.exampleCN: 这座巴洛克教堂以繁复的雕刻闻名。
senses.why: Too much abundance can tip into excess, so the word also judges style as overgrown.
senses.whyCN: 丰盛过了头就会滑向过度，于是这个词也用来评说风格「长得太满」。

intro.en: Exuberant comes from Latin exuberare, to abound, built from ex- and uber, the udder, an image of fertile plenty.
intro.cn: exuberant 来自拉丁语 exuberare（大量涌出、繁盛），由 ex- 与 uber（乳房，丰饶的象征）构成。

items.en: Uber means an animal udder and, by extension, fertile abundance.
items.cn: uber 指动物的乳房，并引申为丰饶多产。

items.en: Most accounts treat ex- here as intensive, though it can also be read as out.
items.cn: 一般认为这里的前缀 ex- 起加强作用，也有解释把它读作「向外」。

items.en: Exuberare means to be very fruitful or to abound.
items.cn: exuberare 意为极为丰产、大量涌出。

items.en: Its participle exuberans supplies the stem of the adjective.
items.cn: 它的分词 exuberans 提供这个形容词的词干。

items.en: French passes the adjective into English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语在十六世纪把这个形容词传入英语。

items.en: English extends it from lush plants to high spirits and rich style.
items.cn: 英语把它从茂盛的植物扩展到高涨的情绪和华丽的风格。

note.en: Exuberant shares the uber root with exuberance and sits near words for lively energy and thick growth.
note.cn: exuberant 与 exuberance 共享 uber 词根，并与表示活泼精力与茂密生长的词相邻。

entries.definition: lively excitement or abundant growth
in an exuberant way
to abound or be exuberant
entries.definitionCN: 繁盛；洋溢（与 exuberant 同源）

entries.definition: full of energy and quick movement
growing thickly and healthily
showing great enthusiasm and energy
entries.definitionCN: 热情奔放的；兴高采烈的

normalIntro.en: Exuberant carries an overflowing image: uber, the udder, suggests milk and plenty running over.
normalIntro.cn: exuberant 带着「满出来」的意象：uber（乳房）暗示奶水与丰盛溢出。

normal.en: Uber is the Latin word for udder, a picture of fertile plenty.
normal.cn: uber 是拉丁语「乳房」，是丰饶多产的画面。

normal.en: The noun is exuberance, and the adverb is exuberantly.
normal.cn: 名词是 exuberance，副词是 exuberantly。

normal.en: Exuberant growth describes plants that burst with leaves.
normal.cn: exuberant growth 形容枝叶疯长的植物。

normal.en: Exuberant fans cheer without holding back.
normal.cn: exuberant fans 指毫不克制地欢呼的粉丝。

normal.en: Compare lush for plants and lively for energy: exuberant covers both plenty and high spirits.
normal.cn: 对比 lush 偏植物、lively 偏精力：exuberant 兼有丰盛与高涨情绪。

abstract.en: See a balloon filled past its size, shining and about to burst with colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一只气球被吹得过满，亮着颜色快要爆开。

abstract.en: Watch a dancer whose energy spills past the edges of the stage.
abstract.cn: 想象一位舞者的劲头漫出舞台边缘。

abstract.en: Picture a wall so covered in vines that no stone shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙被藤蔓盖得看不见石头。

examples.en: The crowd gave the team an exuberant welcome.
examples.cn: 人群给了球队热烈的欢迎。

examples.en: Her exuberant laugh filled the small kitchen.
examples.cn: 她爽朗的笑声充满了小厨房。

examples.en: The garden looked exuberant after weeks of rain.
examples.cn: 下了几周雨，花园看上去一片繁茂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex 读作爱克斯，uber 读作优步」——一出门就叫到车，心情雀跃得溢出来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外，或表加强）+ uber（乳房、丰饶）→ exuberare（大量涌出、繁盛）→ 英语 exuberant；核心义「丰盛得溢出来」。

sensesIntro.en: Exuberant starts with overflowing feeling, moves to energetic action, to thick plant growth, to abundant qualities, and finally to style that has grown too rich.
sensesIntro.cn: exuberant 从满溢的情绪出发，转到有力的动作、茂密的植物、丰富的品质，最后指华丽过头的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plant so full of sap and leaves that it spills over its edges.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株汁液与叶子多到溢出边界的植物。

branches.en: High spirits are the emotional overflow.
branches.cn: 高涨的情绪是情感上的溢出。

branches.en: Vigorous action is the overflow of energy.
branches.cn: 有力的动作是精力上的溢出。

branches.en: Lush growth is the literal image taken from plants.
branches.cn: 茂盛的生长是来自植物的字面意象。

branches.en: Abundant qualities carry the overflow from the physical into the abstract.
branches.cn: 丰富的品质把「满溢」从具体带进抽象。

branches.en: Excess in style is plenty that has gone too far.
branches.cn: 风格上的过度，是丰盛走得太远。

intro.en: Exuberant is a Latin compound of ex- and uber, with English nouns and adverbs built on the same stem.
intro.cn: exuberant 是 ex- 与 uber 的拉丁语复合词，英语在同一词干上构成名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin uber means udder and fertile abundance, and exuberare means to abound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 uber 意为乳房与丰饶，exuberare 意为大量涌出。

items.example: The prefix ex- adds force to the stem.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 为词干加上力度。

items.example: Uber supplies the image of plenty.
items.exampleCN: uber 提供丰盛的意象。

items.example: Ubertas names the quality of plenty.
items.exampleCN: ubertas 指丰盛这一性质。

items.example: Exuberare is the Latin verb behind the word.
items.exampleCN: exuberare 是这个词背后的拉丁动词。

items.example: Exuberantia gives the noun stem.
items.exampleCN: exuberantia 提供名词词干。

items.example: Exuberant keeps the sense of overflow.
items.exampleCN: exuberant 保留了「溢出」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ance forms exuberance.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ance 构成 exuberance。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms exuberantly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 exuberantly。

items.example: The prefix over- forms overexuberant.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 构成 overexuberant。

definition_zh: 渗出；散发；洋溢；流露；分泌
definition_en: to come out slowly through a surface, or to show a quality or feeling so clearly that it seems to pour out of someone
core_image: 冷水瓶壁上，水珠一滴一滴沁出来
scene: 夏天从冰箱里拿出的瓶子放在桌上，瓶壁很快蒙上一层细密的水珠。On a hot day the cold bottle on the table began to exude drops of water within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 exude 是「渗出」（第 1 个义项：液体从表面缓慢沁出）；句意：大热天里，桌上那只冰凉的瓶子几分钟就开始渗出水珠。

pos.zh: 渗出；散发；洋溢；流露（可及物亦可不及物）

derivatives.zh: 由 exude 加名词词尾 -ation 构成，义为「渗出；渗出过程」
由 exude 加名词词尾 -ate 构成，义为「渗出物；渗出液」
由 exudate 加形容词词尾 -ive 构成，义为「渗出性的」

senses.title: To leak out slowly
senses.definition: of a liquid, to come out slowly through the surface of something
senses.definitionCN: 液体从某物的表面缓慢地沁出来
senses.example: The cut on his arm exuded a little blood.
senses.exampleCN: 他手臂上的伤口渗出一点血。
senses.why: The Latin verb sudare means to sweat, so the first picture is liquid sweating out of a surface one drop at a time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 sudare 意为出汗，所以最初的画面是液体像出汗一样一点一点从表面沁出来。

senses.title: To send out a smell or a vapour
senses.definition: to send out a smell, moisture, or vapour over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间里持续散发出气味、湿气或蒸气
senses.example: Crushed pine needles exuded a clean, sharp scent.
senses.exampleCN: 碾碎的松针散发出清冽的气味。
senses.why: Once a surface can sweat, anything that leaves it slowly can be said to exude, and smells are the easiest of these to imagine.
senses.whyCN: 既然表面能「出汗」，任何缓慢离开表面的东西都能用 exude，而气味是最容易想象的一种。

senses.title: To show a quality very clearly
senses.definition: of a person or a place, to show a quality so strongly that it seems to come out of them
senses.definitionCN: 人或地方把某种品质显露得极为充分，仿佛从身上溢出来
senses.example: The old library exuded a quiet dignity.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老图书馆洋溢着一种安静的庄严。
senses.why: A quality such as confidence behaves like that liquid: it cannot be kept inside and seems to seep through the person.
senses.whyCN: 自信这类品质正像那种液体：藏不住，仿佛从人身上渗出来。

senses.title: To reveal a feeling without words
senses.definition: to let an emotion or an attitude be seen through appearance, voice, or manner rather than in words
senses.definitionCN: 通过外表、声音或举止而不是言语让人看出某种情感或态度
senses.example: Her letter exuded warmth and gratitude.
senses.exampleCN: 她的信里流露着温暖与感激。
senses.why: A feeling is even more liquid than a quality, because it leaks through the face and the voice before any words are chosen.
senses.whyCN: 情感比品质更像液体：还没想好说什么，它就已经从脸色和声音里渗出来了。

senses.title: To give off an atmosphere
senses.definition: of a room, a place, or a gathering, to be full of a particular atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 房间、场所或聚会充满某种特定的气氛
senses.example: The whole hall exuded an air of celebration.
senses.exampleCN: 整个大厅弥漫着庆典的气息。
senses.why: A place can sweat an atmosphere in the same way skin sweats water, which is why rooms and halls can exude.
senses.whyCN: 场所也能像皮肤出汗那样「渗出」气氛，所以除了人，房间和大厅也能用 exude。

senses.title: To produce a natural secretion
senses.definition: of a plant, a wound, or a gland, to produce and release a natural substance
senses.definitionCN: 植物、伤口或腺体产生并释放某种天然物质
senses.example: Fresh resin exuded from the bark of the pine.
senses.exampleCN: 新鲜的树脂从松树皮里渗出来。
senses.why: Resin and sap are the oldest examples, because a tree that sweats resin is the model for the whole word.
senses.whyCN: 树脂与树液是最古老的例子，因为「树在出树脂」正是整个词的模型。

senses.title: To cause something to leak out
senses.definition: to cause a liquid or a substance to come out of something, as in medical and technical writing
senses.definitionCN: 使液体或物质从某物中渗出，用于医学与技术写作
senses.example: The nurse noted that the wound exuded clear fluid onto the dressing.
senses.exampleCN: 护士注意到伤口把清亮的液体渗到了敷料上。
senses.why: Because the verb is both transitive and intransitive, the same sweat image can be turned around to focus on what is made to come out.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词既可及物也可不及物，同一个「出汗」意象可以翻转过来，把焦点放在被渗出的东西上。

intro.en: Exude is generally traced to Latin exsudare, also written exudare, from ex-, out, and sudare, to sweat.
intro.cn: exude 一般认为来自拉丁语 exsudare（也写作 exudare），由 ex-（向外）与 sudare（出汗）构成。

items.en: Sudare means to sweat, and the related noun sudor means sweat.
items.cn: sudare 意为出汗，相关名词 sudor 意为汗。

items.en: Exsudare joins ex-, out, with sudare, so the liquid is imagined as sweating out of a surface.
items.cn: exsudare 把 ex-（向外）与 sudare 结合，液体被想象成从表面「出汗」而出。

items.en: Pliny and other writers use the verb for resin and moisture coming out of trees and stone.
items.cn: 普林尼等作家用这个动词描写树脂与湿气从树木和石头中渗出。

items.en: Medical Latin keeps the verb for fluid that leaves a wound or a swollen part of the body.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语沿用这个动词，指液体从伤口或肿胀部位流出。

items.en: English exude appears in the seventeenth century, first in scientific writing about minerals and plants.
items.cn: 英语 exude 在十七世纪出现，最早见于关于矿物与植物的科学写作。

items.en: Modern English extends the verb to confidence, charm, and atmosphere, where nothing physical comes out.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个动词扩展到自信、魅力与气氛，此时并没有任何实体渗出。

note.en: Exude belongs to the Latin sweating family of sudare, and its near meanings are verbs of emitting and radiating.
note.cn: exude 属于拉丁语 sudare（出汗）这一词族，近义方向是「排放、辐射」类动词。

entries.definition: the substance that has seeped out of a body or a surface
entries.definitionCN: 从身体或表面渗出的物质，与 exude 同源，是「渗出来的东西」的名词形式

entries.definition: the slow seeping out of a liquid
entries.definitionCN: 液体的缓慢渗出，由 exude 加 -ation 构成的过程名词

entries.definition: causing a person to sweat
entries.definitionCN: 使人发汗的，与 exude 共享拉丁语 sudor（汗）这一词根

entries.definition: to send out light, heat, sound, or a gas
entries.definitionCN: 发出（光、热、声、气体），偏物理，不含「慢慢沁出」的意味

entries.definition: to send out heat, light, or a feeling from a central point
entries.definitionCN: 辐射；散发出（热、光或某种感觉），强调由中心向外扩散

entries.definition: to flow out very slowly, often through small openings
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢流出，常指从细缝中渗出，与 exude 的物理义项最接近

normalIntro.en: Exude is built from the Latin sweat family, and its senses all keep the idea of something leaving a surface slowly.
normalIntro.cn: exude 由拉丁语「出汗」词族构成，各义项都保留「某物缓慢离开表面」这一想法。

normal.en: Ex- means out and sudare means to sweat, so exude is to sweat something out.
normal.cn: ex- 表示向外，sudare 表示出汗，所以 exude 就是让某物像出汗一样出来。

normal.en: Liquids, smells, and moods all exude, because all of them can leave a surface slowly.
normal.cn: 液体、气味、情绪都能 exude，因为它们都能从表面缓慢离开。

normal.en: The pattern exude confidence covers the quality sense in one phrase.
normal.cn: 搭配「exude confidence」一句话就覆盖了品质义项。

normal.en: A damp wall exudes moisture after rain, which is the plain physical sense.
normal.cn: 雨后潮湿的墙会 exude moisture，这是最朴素的物理义项。

normal.en: Exudate is the noun for whatever has come out.
normal.cn: exudate 是名词，指渗出来的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a cold glass beading with water in a warm room.
abstract.cn: 想象温暖房间里一只冷杯子挂满水珠。

abstract.en: Picture crushed pine needles filling the air with a clean scent.
abstract.cn: 想象碾碎的松针让空气里满是清冽的气味。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose calm seems to pour out of the sleeves.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人，沉静仿佛从袖口里淌出来。

examples.en: The leaves exude a sticky sap when they are bruised.
examples.cn: 叶子被碰伤时会渗出黏黏的树液。

examples.en: The old library exuded a quiet dignity.
examples.cn: 这座老图书馆洋溢着安静的庄严。

examples.en: Fresh resin exuded from the bark of the pine.
examples.cn: 新鲜的树脂从松树皮里渗出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音近「伊克苏德」，可联想「一宿的」雨让墙缝渗出湿气——只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ sudare（出汗）→ exsudare（渗出、出汗而出）→ 英语 exude，核心义「像出汗一样从表面沁出」。

sensesIntro.en: Exude starts with liquid sweating out of a surface, moves to smells and vapours, then to qualities, feelings, and whole atmospheres, and keeps a technical sense for resin and other secretions.
sensesIntro.cn: exude 从液体像出汗一样沁出表面开始，转到气味与蒸气，再转到品质、情感与整个气氛，同时保留树脂等分泌物的技术义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: liquid sweating out of a surface, one drop at a time.
core.cn: 核心意象：液体像出汗一样，一滴一滴从表面沁出。

branches.en: Liquid leaving a surface is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 液体离开表面，是物理义项。

branches.en: Smell and vapour are the next thing to sweat out.
branches.cn: 气味与蒸气是接着「渗出」的东西。

branches.en: Qualities and feelings act like liquid that cannot stay inside.
branches.cn: 品质与情感就像藏不住的液体。

branches.en: A place sweats an atmosphere instead of water.
branches.cn: 场所渗出的不是水，而是气氛。

branches.en: Resin and other secretions keep the technical and transitive uses alive.
branches.cn: 树脂等分泌物让技术义项与及物用法延续下来。

intro.en: Exude is built on the Latin prefix ex- and the sweating verb sudare, and English has kept a small family around it.
intro.cn: exude 建立在拉丁语前缀 ex- 与表示「出汗」的 sudare 之上，英语围绕它保留了一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin sudare means to sweat, sudor means sweat, and exsudare means to sweat out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sudare 意为出汗，sudor 意为汗，exsudare 意为渗出。

items.example: The prefix ex- turns a verb of sweating into a verb of sweating out.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 把「出汗」的动词变成「出汗而出、渗出」的动词。

items.example: Sudare supplies the sweating image behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: sudare 提供整个词族背后「出汗」的意象。

items.example: Sudor survives in English in sudorific and sudoriferous.
items.exampleCN: sudor 在英语的 sudorific 与 sudoriferous 中留存下来。

items.meaning: to sweat out, to seep out
items.example: Exsudare is usually given as the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: exsudare 通常被认为是英语 exude 的直接来源。

items.example: Exudation names the process rather than the thing.
items.exampleCN: exudation 指渗出这个过程，而不是渗出的东西。

items.meaning: the substance that has seeped out
items.example: Exudate is what a wound leaves on the dressing.
items.exampleCN: exudate 就是伤口留在敷料上的渗出物。

items.example: Doctors describe some skin conditions as exudative.
items.exampleCN: 医生把某些皮肤状况描述为渗出性的。

items.example: Sudorific medicines were once used to bring on a sweat.
items.exampleCN: 发汗药过去常用来让人出汗。

items.example: Sudoriferous glands are the ones that produce sweat.
items.exampleCN: sudoriferous 修饰的腺体就是分泌汗液的那些腺体。

definition_zh: 欢欣鼓舞；狂喜；得意；欢跃
definition_en: to feel and show great happiness, especially after a success or good news, as if the joy makes you jump
core_image: 听到喜讯的人一跃而起，双臂高高举起
scene: 球赛最后一分钟进球，看台上的球迷全都跳了起来。When the team scored in the final minute, the fans in the stands exulted and hugged one another.
sceneCN: 这里 exult 是「欢欣鼓舞」（第 1 个义项：因成功或喜讯而极度欢喜）；句意：球队在最后一分钟进球时，看台上的球迷欢腾跳跃，互相拥抱。

pos.zh: 欢欣鼓舞；狂喜；得意；欢跃

derivatives.zh: 由 exult 加形容词词尾 -ant 构成，义为「欢欣鼓舞的；得意洋洋的」
由 exult 加名词词尾 -ation 构成，义为「狂喜；欢腾」
由 exultant 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「得意洋洋地」

senses.title: To rejoice greatly
senses.definition: to feel and express great joy, especially because of a success or good news
senses.definitionCN: 因成功或喜讯而感到并表现出极大的喜悦
senses.example: The pupils exulted when the school announced an extra holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 学校宣布多放一天假时，学生们欢欣雀跃。
senses.why: Latin exsultare means to leap up, so the joy in exult is not a quiet feeling but a jump.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 exsultare 意为跳起来，所以 exult 的喜悦不是静静的感受，而是一跳。

senses.title: To celebrate a victory openly
senses.definition: to celebrate a win or an achievement with visible excitement in front of others
senses.definitionCN: 在众人面前以看得见的兴奋庆祝胜利或成就
senses.example: The players exulted on the pitch after the final whistle.
senses.exampleCN: 终场哨响后，球员们在球场上欢庆胜利。
senses.why: The leap of joy naturally becomes public when a whole team or crowd jumps together, and that shared jump is celebration.
senses.whyCN: 当整支队伍或整群观众一起跳起来，喜悦的一跃自然变成公开的庆祝。

senses.title: To be triumphant over someone
senses.definition: to show proud satisfaction, especially at the defeat or weakness of another person
senses.definitionCN: 表现出得意的满足，尤指因他人失败或软弱而得意
senses.example: He exulted over the blunder of his rival.
senses.exampleCN: 他因对手的失误而得意洋洋。
senses.why: A jump can also be a jump on top of someone else, and the verb takes that darker colour when the joy is fed by another person losing.
senses.whyCN: 一跃也可以踩在别人身上，当喜悦来自他人落败时，这个词就带上这层暗色。

senses.title: To delight in something
senses.definition: to take great pleasure in an activity, a state, or a possession
senses.definitionCN: 从某种活动、状态或所拥有的东西中获得极大乐趣
senses.example: She exulted in the freedom of a long summer.
senses.exampleCN: 她陶醉于漫长夏日的自由之中。
senses.why: The object of joy can be a thing rather than a victory, and the pattern exult in marks that everyday delight.
senses.whyCN: 喜悦的对象可以不是胜利，而是某样东西，「exult in」这一搭配正标记这种日常的陶醉。

senses.title: To leap for joy
senses.definition: to jump about in joy, used especially in religious and literary writing
senses.definitionCN: 因喜悦而跳跃，尤用于宗教与文学文本
senses.example: In the old hymn, the hills exult before the Lord.
senses.exampleCN: 这首赞美诗呼唤群山在主面前欢跃。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is the physical leap, and religious language keeps it because praise there is acted out with the whole body.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层就是身体的一跃，宗教语言保留它，因为那里的赞美是用整个身体做出来的。

intro.en: Exult comes, probably through French, from Latin exsultare, to leap up, built on ex-, out and up, and saltare, to jump.
intro.cn: exult 一般认为经由法语来自拉丁语 exsultare（跳起来），由 ex-（向外、向上）与 saltare（跳跃）构成。

items.en: Salire means to leap, and saltare, its frequentative, means to jump again and again or to dance.
items.cn: salire 意为跳跃，其反复动词 saltare 意为反复跳、舞蹈。

items.en: Exsultare adds ex- and first means to spring up or bound, then to rejoice wildly.
items.cn: exsultare 加上 ex-，先表示弹起、蹦跳，再表示狂喜。

items.en: Cicero and Virgil use exsultare for leaping animals and for people carried away by joy.
items.cn: 西塞罗与维吉尔用 exsultare 描写蹦跳的动物，也描写被喜悦冲昏的人。

items.en: Old French exulter carries the joy sense forward and drops the written s of exsultare.
items.cn: 古法语 exulter 把喜悦义继续往下传，并丢掉了 exsultare 中不发音的 s。

items.en: English first records the noun exultation, the mood of leaping joy.
items.cn: 英语先记录名词 exultation，即「跳跃般的喜悦」这种心境。

items.en: The verb exult appears in the sixteenth century, most likely shortened from exultation, and keeps the leap inside the joy.
items.cn: 动词 exult 在十六世纪出现，一般认为是 exultation 的缩短形式，并把「跳跃」这一意象留在喜悦之中。

note.en: Exult shares the Latin root salire, to leap, with insult, result, and assault, and is easily confused with exalt.
note.cn: exult 与拉丁语 salire（跳）同根，insult、result、assault 都出自这个词根，它又容易与 exalt 混淆。

entries.definition: to praise someone highly or to raise them to a higher rank
entries.definitionCN: 赞扬；提升，与 exult 只是拼写和读音相近，词源不同：exalt 出自拉丁语 altus（高）

entries.definition: feeling or showing great joy and triumph
entries.definitionCN: 欢欣鼓舞的；得意洋洋的，由 exult 加 -ant 构成的形容词

entries.definition: a feeling of great joy and triumph
entries.definitionCN: 狂喜；欢腾，由 exult 加 -ation 构成的名词

entries.definition: to feel or show great joy
entries.definitionCN: 欢喜；高兴，是最中性的「喜悦」动词，不含跳跃的画面

entries.definition: to mark a happy event with a party or a ceremony
entries.definitionCN: 庆祝，强调用活动或仪式标记喜事

entries.definition: to enjoy oneself in a lively and noisy way
entries.definitionCN: 尽情作乐；狂欢，比 exult 更强调喧闹的享乐

normalIntro.en: Exult is joy with a jump inside it, because its Latin root is the verb to leap.
normalIntro.cn: exult 是带着跳跃的喜悦，因为它的拉丁词根就是「跳」这个动词。

normal.en: Ex- plus saltare, to jump: exult is joy that jumps.
normal.cn: ex- 加 saltare（跳）：exult 就是会跳起来的喜悦。

normal.en: The noun exultation names the mood, and the adjective exultant describes the person.
normal.cn: 名词 exultation 指这种心境，形容词 exultant 描述处于这种心境的人。

normal.en: Exult at the news and exult over a victory are the two common frames.
normal.cn: 「exult at the news」与「exult over a victory」是两个常见框架。

normal.en: Exult over a rival carries a hint of gloating, so use it with care.
normal.cn: 「exult over a rival」带一点幸灾乐祸，用时要小心。

normal.en: Compare exalt: exalt raises a person, exult only jumps.
normal.cn: 对比 exalt：exalt 把人抬高，exult 只是跳。

abstract.en: Picture a fan springing up when the final whistle blows.
abstract.cn: 想象终场哨响时，一名球迷从座位上弹起来。

abstract.en: Picture a team lifting the trophy and running round the pitch.
abstract.cn: 想象一支队伍举起奖杯，绕着球场奔跑。

abstract.en: Picture someone smiling at a rival who has just failed.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人对着刚刚失败的对手露出笑容。

examples.en: The children exulted when the first snow came.
examples.cn: 第一场雪落下时，孩子们欢腾起来。

examples.en: The captain exulted over the unexpected win.
examples.cn: 队长为这场意外的胜利而狂喜。

examples.en: She exulted in the quiet of the early morning.
examples.cn: 她沉醉于清晨的宁静之中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音近「伊克搜特」，可联想人一高兴就「嗖」地跳起来——只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、向上）+ salire（跳）→ exsultare（跳起来、欢腾）→ 古法语 exulter → 英语 exult，核心义「高兴得跳起来」。

sensesIntro.en: Exult begins with joy that jumps, then widens to public celebration of a win, to triumph over a rival, to delight in anything, and finally to the literal leaping of religious and literary writing.
sensesIntro.cn: exult 从「会跳的喜悦」开始，扩展到公开庆祝胜利、因压过对手而得意、以某事为乐，最后回到宗教与文学中字面意义上的欢跃。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person springing up with both arms raised.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人一跃而起，双臂高高举起。

branches.en: Great joy is the inner feeling of the jump.
branches.cn: 巨大的喜悦是这一跃的内在感受。

branches.en: A crowd jumping together turns the feeling into celebration.
branches.cn: 一群人一起跳，就把感受变成庆祝。

branches.en: Jumping on a defeated rival gives the triumphal and gloating sense.
branches.cn: 踩在落败对手身上跳，生出得意与幸灾乐祸的义项。

branches.en: The jump can also be a jump of pleasure in a thing or a state.
branches.cn: 这一跃也可以是为某物、某种状态而雀跃。

branches.en: Religious writing keeps the literal leap of the body.
branches.cn: 宗教文本保留身体字面意义上的欢跃。

intro.en: Exult is built on ex- and the leap root salire, which also gives English insult, result, and assault.
intro.cn: exult 建立在 ex- 与表示「跳」的词根 salire 上，英语的 insult、result、assault 也出自这个词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin salire means to leap, saltare means to jump repeatedly, and exsultare means to leap up with joy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 salire 意为跳跃，saltare 意为反复跳，exsultare 意为欢跃而起。

items.example: The prefix ex- lifts the jump into a jump of joy.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 把一次跳跃抬成喜悦的跳跃。

items.example: Salire is the plain leap at the bottom of the family.
items.exampleCN: salire 是这个词族最底层、最朴素的一跳。

items.example: Saltare turns one leap into a dance.
items.exampleCN: saltare 把一次跳跃变成一支舞。

items.example: Exsultare joins the leap with the joy.
items.exampleCN: exsultare 把跳跃与喜悦结合在一起。

items.example: Exult is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: exult 是简短的英语动词。

items.example: The suffix -ant turns exult into exultant.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 把 exult 变成 exultant。

items.example: The suffix -ation turns exult into exultation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 把 exult 变成 exultation。

items.example: Exulting crowds filled the square.
items.exampleCN: 欢腾的人群挤满了广场。

items.meaning: to speak to or treat someone with contempt
items.example: Insult comes from in- plus salire, to jump at.
items.exampleCN: insult 来自 in- 加 salire，意为「朝某人跳过去」。

items.example: Result comes from re- plus salire, to spring back.
items.exampleCN: result 来自 re- 加 salire，意为「弹回来」。

definition_zh: 视力；视野；眼光
definition_en: the ability to see; the range within which you can see; the ability to judge
core_image: 远处字母表在眼前逐渐清晰或模糊
scene: 随着年龄增长，他的视力变差了。His eyesight grew worse with age.
sceneCN: 这里 eyesight 是「视力」（第 1 个义项）；句意：随着年龄增长，他的视力变差了。

derivatives.zh: 眼睛
视力；景象
有视力的
近视的；目光短浅的

senses.title: The ability to see
senses.definition: the ability of the eyes to see
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛观看的能力
senses.example: Good eyesight is important for driving.
senses.exampleCN: 好视力对开车很重要。
senses.why: The core sense is the power of the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是眼睛的观看能力。

senses.title: Range of vision
senses.definition: the distance within which things can be seen
senses.definitionCN: 能够看见事物的距离范围
senses.example: The plane disappeared from eyesight.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机从视野中消失了。
senses.why: The ability becomes the range it covers.
senses.whyCN: 能力变成它所覆盖的范围。

senses.title: Judgment
senses.definition: the ability to judge or notice things well
senses.definitionCN: 善于判断或察觉事物的能力
senses.example: His business eyesight is respected.
senses.exampleCN: 他的商业眼光受人尊敬。
senses.why: Physical sight becomes mental insight.
senses.whyCN: 身体上的视觉变成心智上的洞察。

intro.en: Eyesight joins eye and sight, two Old English words for seeing.
intro.cn: eyesight 由 eye 与 sight 组成，两者都是古英语中与「看」有关的词。

items.en: Eage names the organ of sight.
items.cn: eage 指观看的器官。

items.en: Sihth names the act or power of seeing.
items.cn: sihth 指看的动作或能力。

items.en: The two words join to name the power of the eyes.
items.cn: 两个词组合起来指眼睛的能力。

items.en: Eyesight becomes the common word for vision.
items.cn: 中古英语中 eyesight 成为表示视力的常用词。

items.en: Eyesight also covers range and judgment.
items.cn: 现代英语中 eyesight 也涵盖视野与眼光。

note.en: Eyesight is the power to see; insight is deep understanding.
note.cn: eyesight 是看的能力，insight 则是深刻的理解。

entries.definition: a deep understanding of something
the ability to see
something ugly to look at
the ability to see
the power or act of seeing
what can be seen from a place

normalIntro.en: Eyesight is the power of the eyes to see clearly.
normalIntro.cn: eyesight 是眼睛清楚观看的能力。

normal.en: His eyesight is poor without glasses.
normal.cn: 不戴眼镜时他的视力很差。

normal.en: The test checks the eyesight of drivers.
normal.cn: 这项测试检查司机的视力。

normal.en: She lost her eyesight in one eye.
normal.cn: 她一只眼睛失明了。

normal.en: Good eyesight helped him spot the bird.
normal.cn: 好视力让他发现了那只鸟。

normal.en: Failing eyesight made reading difficult.
normal.cn: 视力衰退让阅读变得困难。

abstract.en: Picture letters on a chart fading into blur.
abstract.cn: 想象视力表上的字母渐渐变模糊。

abstract.en: Imagine a distant ship slowly leaving view.
abstract.cn: 想象远处的船慢慢离开视野。

abstract.en: Think of a sharp image coming into focus.
abstract.cn: 想象清晰的画面逐渐对焦。

examples.en: Regular tests can protect your eyesight.
examples.cn: 定期检查可以保护视力。

examples.en: His eyesight is still sharp at eighty.
examples.cn: 他八十岁视力仍然敏锐。

examples.en: The bird flew out of eyesight.
examples.cn: 鸟儿飞出了视野。

dict_mnemonic.text: eye（眼睛）加 sight（看），两者合起来就是眼睛看的能力，即 eyesight（视力）。

root: 由 eye 与 sight 复合而成，两者都源自古英语中与「看」有关的词，核心义「眼睛的观看能力」。

sensesIntro.en: Eyesight means the ability to see, the range of vision, or good judgment.
sensesIntro.cn: eyesight 意为观看能力、视野范围，或良好的判断力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: letters coming into focus on a chart.
core.cn: 核心意象：视力表上的字母逐渐清晰。

branches.en: The base sense is the power to see.
branches.cn: 基础义是观看的能力。

branches.en: The ability becomes the range it covers.
branches.cn: 能力变成它所覆盖的范围。

branches.en: Physical sight becomes mental judgment.
branches.cn: 身体视觉变成心智判断。

branches.en: Clear sight and wide range support each other.
branches.cn: 清晰视力与宽广视野相互支持。

branches.en: Seeing well and judging well share the eye.
branches.cn: 看得清与判断准都离不开眼睛。

intro.en: Eyesight is a compound of two native English words about seeing.
intro.cn: eyesight 由两个表示「看」的英语本族词复合而成。

latinIntro.en: Eyesight has no Latin root; both parts are Old English.
latinIntro.cn: eyesight 没有拉丁词根，两个部分都来自古英语。

items.example: His eyesight is excellent.
items.exampleCN: 他的视力很好。

items.example: The eye needs rest.
items.exampleCN: 眼睛需要休息。

items.example: Sight is one of the five senses.
items.exampleCN: 视觉是五种感官之一。

items.example: The center helps sighted and blind people.
items.exampleCN: 这个中心帮助视力正常者与盲人。

items.example: He is short-sighted in one eye.
items.exampleCN: 他一只眼睛近视。

items.meaning: unable to see near things clearly
items.example: She is long-sighted and needs glasses.
items.exampleCN: 她远视，需要戴眼镜。

items.example: A clear-sighted leader plans ahead.
items.exampleCN: 头脑清醒的领导者会提前规划。

items.example: The book gives insight into history.
items.exampleCN: 这本书让人深入了解历史。

items.example: The plan shows great foresight.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划显示出远见。

definition_zh: 目击者；见证人；目击证词；亲眼所见
definition_en: a person who sees an event happen and can describe it from direct observation
core_image: 一个人站在街角，睁大眼睛看着事故全过程
scene: 路口两车相撞，一位等公交的女士把整个过程看得清清楚楚。A woman waiting for the bus saw the whole crash and later described it to the police as an eyewitness.
sceneCN: 这里 eyewitness 是「目击者」（第 1 个义项：亲眼看到事件发生的人）；句意：一位等公交的女士看见了两车相撞的全过程，后来以目击者身份向警方描述。

pos.zh: 目击者；见证人（也作定语，如目击证词）

derivatives.zh: 复合词的核心成分，独立表示「证人；证词」，也可作动词表示「目睹」
仿 eye 加 witness 构成，指只凭听说而非亲眼所见的人，与 eyewitness 相对
较早的连字符写法，与 eyewitness 同义，多见于十九世纪及以前的报刊文本

senses.title: A person who saw it happen
senses.definition: a person who was present when an event happened and saw it with his or her own eyes
senses.definitionCN: 事件发生时在场并亲眼看到的人
senses.example: The police are looking for an eyewitness to the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 警方正在寻找这起事故的目击者。
senses.why: The compound joins eye, the organ that sees, with witness, the person who can tell what happened, so the word is a seeing person who can speak.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把「看的器官」eye 与「能讲述发生什么的人」witness 结合，所以它指一个看见了又能说出来的人。

senses.title: A witness who gives evidence
senses.definition: a person who saw an event and is called to describe it in a court or an official inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 看到事件并被传唤到法庭或官方调查中描述经过的人
senses.example: Two eyewitnesses gave evidence at the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 两名目击证人在庭审中作证。
senses.why: Witness already carries the legal sense of testimony, so an eyewitness in court is both the pair of eyes and the voice under oath.
senses.whyCN: witness 本身就有「证词」的法律含义，所以法庭上的 eyewitness 既是那双眼，也是宣誓后的声音。

senses.title: An account given by a witness
senses.definition: the story or description that such a person gives, used before nouns such as account and report
senses.definitionCN: 目击者给出的叙述或描述，常用作 account、report 等名词的定语
senses.example: The report is based on eyewitness accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇报道依据的是目击者的叙述。
senses.why: Once the person is named, the words that person produces take the same label, so an eyewitness account is the account of an eyewitness.
senses.whyCN: 人既有了名号，这个人说出的话也沿用同一标签，所以 eyewitness account 就是目击者的叙述。

senses.title: Identification by a witness
senses.definition: the act of a witness picking out a person, especially a suspect, as the one seen at the event
senses.definitionCN: 目击者指认出在事件现场看到的人，尤指指认嫌疑人
senses.example: The court questioned the reliability of eyewitness identification.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭对目击辨认的可靠性提出质疑。
senses.why: The seeing and the naming meet in identification, where the eyes of the witness are asked to point at a face in a line of strangers.
senses.whyCN: 「看见」与「指认」在辨认这里会合：目击者的眼睛要在一排陌生人里指出一张脸。

senses.title: A witness to history
senses.definition: a person who was present at a great public event and can testify to it afterwards
senses.definitionCN: 亲历重大公共事件、事后可以为其作证的人
senses.example: She was an eyewitness to the fall of the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 她是那堵墙倒塌的见证人。
senses.why: History is treated as an event that happens in front of somebody, so the plain seeing person becomes a witness to a whole age.
senses.whyCN: 历史被当作在某人眼前发生的事件，于是那个朴素的「看见的人」就成了整个时代的见证人。

intro.en: Eyewitness is an English compound of eye and witness, and witness itself goes back to Old English witnes, knowledge or testimony.
intro.cn: eyewitness 是 eye 与 witness 构成的英语复合词，而 witness 本身可追溯到古英语 witnes（知识、证词）。

items.en: Eage means eye, and wit means knowledge or understanding.
items.cn: eage 意为眼睛，wit 意为知识、理解。

items.en: Witnes means testimony, and also the person who gives it, formed with the noun suffix -nes.
items.cn: witnes 意为证词，也指提供证词的人，由名词词尾 -nes 构成。

items.en: Eye and witness are both common words, but they are not yet joined into one.
items.cn: 中古英语里 eye 与 witness 都是常用词，但还没有合成一个词。

items.en: Eyewitness is recorded in the sixteenth century for a person who saw an event himself or herself.
items.cn: eyewitness 在十六世纪被记录，指亲自看到事件的人。

items.en: Courts and newspapers begin to use the word before nouns, as in eyewitness account and eyewitness testimony.
items.cn: 十九世纪，法庭与报纸开始把这个词放在名词前，如目击叙述与目击证词。

items.en: Modern English adds eyewitness identification and eyewitness footage to the legal and media family.
items.cn: 现代英语又给法律与媒体词族加上「目击辨认」与「目击影像」。

note.en: Eyewitness is a transparent compound, so its closest words are witness, earwitness, and the seeing eye itself, with observers and bystanders as near meanings.
note.cn: eyewitness 是个一看就懂的复合词，最近的词是 witness、earwitness 与「看的眼睛」本身，近义方向则是旁观者一类。

entries.definition: a person who sees an event or gives evidence about it
entries.definitionCN: 证人；目击者，是 eyewitness 的核心成分，但不强调「亲眼看见」

entries.definition: a person who reports an event from hearing rather than seeing it
entries.definitionCN: 耳闻者，仿 eyewitness 构成，指只凭听觉转述事件的人，与「目击」相对

entries.definition: the organ of sight
entries.definitionCN: 眼睛，是复合词的第一部分，也是「亲眼」这层意思的来源

entries.definition: a person who watches something carefully, often by design
entries.definitionCN: 观察者，强调有意识地注视，不一定是事件的当事人

entries.definition: a person who is present at an event but does not take part in it
entries.definitionCN: 旁观者；路人，强调在场却不介入，常与「见死不救」的议论相连

entries.definition: a person who watches something happening without joining in
entries.definitionCN: 围观者，偏口语，强调看热闹的位置

normalIntro.en: Eyewitness is a compound that anyone can read: the eye supplies the seeing and witness supplies the testimony.
normalIntro.cn: eyewitness 是个谁都能读懂的复合词：eye 提供「看见」，witness 提供「证词」。

normal.en: Eye plus witness: the eye does the seeing, the witness does the telling.
normal.cn: eye 加 witness：眼睛负责看见，witness 负责讲述。

normal.en: Witness alone can be a person in court, while eyewitness stresses that the person was there and saw it.
normal.cn: 单说 witness 可以是法庭上的证人，而 eyewitness 强调此人当时在场、亲眼看见。

normal.en: An eyewitness account is the story that such a person tells.
normal.cn: eyewitness account 就是这种目击者讲出来的经过。

normal.en: Earwitness is the rare opposite, built for someone who only heard about the event.
normal.cn: earwitness 是罕见的反面构词，专指只听说过事件的人。

normal.en: Police appeals often ask eyewitnesses to come forward.
normal.cn: 警方通告常常请目击者站出来提供线索。

abstract.en: Picture a woman on the corner watching two cars slide into each other.
abstract.cn: 想象一位女士站在街角，看着两辆车撞在一起。

abstract.en: Picture the same woman in a courtroom, asked to point at a face.
abstract.cn: 想象同一位女士坐在法庭里，被要求指出一张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook where she writes down every detail she saw.
abstract.cn: 想象一个本子，她把看到的每个细节都记下来。

examples.en: Several eyewitnesses described the man leaving the building.
examples.cn: 几名目击者描述了那名男子离开大楼的经过。

examples.en: The police are looking for an eyewitness to the accident.
examples.cn: 警方正在寻找这起事故的目击者。

examples.en: The article quotes an eyewitness account of the flood.
examples.cn: 这篇文章引用了目击者对那场洪水的叙述。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱」与「威特尼斯」连读——「爱」用眼睛盯住现场的人，就是目击者；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 eage（眼睛）+ witnes（证词、见证，源自 wit「知道」）→ eyewitness，核心义「亲眼看见并且能够作证的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Eyewitness names the person first, then the legal witness, then the account that person gives, then identification, and finally the witness to a whole age.
sensesIntro.cn: eyewitness 先指那个人，再指法律意义上的证人，继而指此人给出的叙述、指认行为，最后指整个时代的见证人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing at the scene with eyes open, watching it happen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在现场，睁大眼睛看着事情发生。

branches.en: The seeing person at the scene is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 在现场看见的那个人，是最基本的义项。

branches.en: Being present becomes formal when the witness must testify.
branches.cn: 当证人必须作证时，「在场」就变成正式的法律身份。

branches.en: The words of the witness take the same name as the witness.
branches.cn: 证人说出的内容沿用了证人本身的名称。

branches.en: The eyes of the witness are asked to pick a face out of a line.
branches.cn: 证人的眼睛被要求在人群中指认一张脸。

branches.en: When the event is huge, the witness becomes a witness to history.
branches.cn: 事件足够重大时，目击者就成了历史的见证人。

intro.en: Eyewitness is a transparent English compound of eye and witness, and English has built a few more compounds on the same model.
intro.cn: eyewitness 是 eye 与 witness 构成的透明复合词，英语还按同一模式造了几个复合词。

latinIntro.en: Eyewitness has no Latin root, because eye and witness are both Old English words; Latin oculus is a distant cognate of eye, and Latin testis names the same role of witness.
latinIntro.cn: eyewitness 没有拉丁词根，因为 eye 与 witness 都是古英语词；拉丁语 oculus 与 eye 同出原始印欧语，testis 则是拉丁语里担任「证人」这一角色的词。

items.example: Eye is the seeing half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: eye 是复合词中「看」的那一半。

items.example: Witness is the speaking half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: witness 是复合词中「讲述」的那一半。

items.example: To witness an event is to be there when it happens.
items.exampleCN: witness 一个事件，就是事件发生时在场。

items.meaning: forms nouns of state or quality
items.meaningCN: 构成状态或性质名词的词尾
items.example: Witnes was built with the noun suffix -nes.
items.exampleCN: witnes 就是用名词词尾 -nes 构成的。

items.meaning: a person who saw an event and can describe it
items.example: Eyewitness puts the two halves together.
items.exampleCN: eyewitness 把这两半合在一起。

items.meaning: more than one person who saw the event
items.example: Eyewitnesses add the plural ending -es.
items.exampleCN: eyewitnesses 加上复数词尾 -es。

items.meaning: a person who only heard about the event
items.example: Earwitness swaps the eye for an ear.
items.exampleCN: earwitness 把眼睛换成了耳朵。

items.meaning: the story told by a person who saw it
items.example: An eyewitness account is the oldest kind of news.
items.exampleCN: 目击者的叙述是最古老的一种新闻。

items.meaning: evidence given in court by a person who saw it
items.example: Eyewitness testimony is powerful but not always accurate.
items.exampleCN: 目击证词很有分量，但并不总是准确。

items.meaning: the act of a witness picking out a suspect
items.example: Eyewitness identification is studied by psychologists.
items.exampleCN: 目击辨认是心理学家研究的对象。

definition_zh: 织物；布料；结构；组织
definition_en: cloth made by weaving or knitting; the structure of a society or system; the way parts are joined
core_image: 经纬线交错织成的一大块布
scene: 这种织物摸起来很柔软。This fabric feels very soft.
sceneCN: 这里 fabric 是「织物、布料」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这种织物摸起来很柔软。

derivatives.zh: 制造；编造
制造；捏造
制造者；捏造者

senses.title: Woven cloth
senses.definition: cloth made by weaving or knitting threads
senses.definitionCN: 由纱线编织或针织成的布
senses.example: The curtains are made of cotton fabric.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘是用棉布做的。
senses.why: The core sense is material made from joined threads.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是由线交织而成的材料。

senses.title: Structure
senses.definition: the way the parts of something are joined together
senses.definitionCN: 事物各部分连接在一起的方式
senses.example: The fabric of the building is still strong.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋建筑的结构仍然坚固。
senses.why: Joined threads become joined parts.
senses.whyCN: 交织的线变成连接的结构。

senses.title: The social system
senses.definition: the basic structure of a society or group
senses.definitionCN: 社会或群体的基本结构
senses.example: Trust holds the social fabric together.
senses.exampleCN: 信任维系着社会结构。
senses.why: A woven surface becomes the web of society.
senses.whyCN: 织成的表面变成社会之网。

intro.en: Fabric comes from Latin fabrica, a workshop or craft, from faber, a worker.
intro.cn: fabric 来自拉丁语 fabrica（作坊、技艺），根源是 faber（工匠）。

items.en: Faber means a worker or craftsman.
items.cn: faber 意为工匠。

items.en: Fabrica means a workshop or craft.
items.cn: fabrica 意为作坊或技艺。

items.en: Fabricare means to make or build.
items.cn: fabricare 意为制作或建造。

items.en: Fabric reaches English through French.
items.cn: fabric 经法语进入英语。

items.en: Fabric means cloth and also a structure.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fabric 既指布料也指结构。

note.en: Fabric is cloth or structure; fabricate is to make up.
note.cn: fabric 是织物或结构，fabricate 则是制造或捏造。

entries.definition: to make or invent something
extremely good
a thin thread used in cloth
material made from threads
woven or knitted cloth
the way parts are arranged

normalIntro.en: Fabric is woven cloth and also the woven structure of a society.
normalIntro.cn: fabric 是织成的布，也指社会织成的结构。

normal.en: This fabric is soft and light.
normal.cn: 这种织物柔软轻便。

normal.en: The shop sells fabric by the meter.
normal.cn: 这家店按米卖布料。

normal.en: The old fabric of the city is changing.
normal.cn: 这座城市旧的结构正在改变。

normal.en: Poverty can damage the social fabric.
normal.cn: 贫困会损害社会结构。

normal.en: They chose a strong fabric for the curtains.
normal.cn: 他们为窗帘选了结实的布料。

abstract.en: Picture threads crossing over and under each other.
abstract.cn: 想象线一根根上下交错。

abstract.en: Imagine a city held together by many small ties.
abstract.cn: 想象城市被许多细小纽带连在一起。

abstract.en: Think of a net whose knots support the whole.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网，每个结都支撑整体。

examples.en: The dress is made from a light fabric.
examples.cn: 这条裙子用轻薄的布料做成。

examples.en: Trust is part of the fabric of a team.
examples.cn: 信任是团队结构的一部分。

examples.en: The fabric of the old house is still sound.
examples.cn: 老房子的结构仍然完好。

dict_mnemonic.text: fabric 与 fabricate 同源：先有「制作」，再指制作出的织物与结构。

root: 源自拉丁语 fabrica（作坊、技艺），由 faber（工匠）派生，核心义「制作出来的织物与结构」。

sensesIntro.en: Fabric means woven cloth, the way parts are joined, or the structure of a society.
sensesIntro.cn: fabric 意为织成的布、部件的连接方式，或社会结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: threads woven into one strong sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：线交织成一整块结实的布。

branches.en: The base sense is woven cloth.
branches.cn: 基础义是织成的布。

branches.en: Joined threads become joined parts.
branches.cn: 交织的线变成连接的结构。

branches.en: A woven surface becomes the web of society.
branches.cn: 织成的表面变成社会之网。

branches.en: Cloth and building structure both depend on joining.
branches.cn: 布料与建筑结构都依赖连接。

branches.en: Material structure and social structure share a frame.
branches.cn: 物质结构与社会结构共享一个框架。

intro.en: Fabric belongs to the Latin faber family, like fabricate and fabrication.
intro.cn: fabric 属于拉丁语 faber 词族，与 fabricate、fabrication 同源。

latinIntro.en: Latin fabrica, fabricare, and faber are the source forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fabrica、fabricare 与 faber 是来源形式。

items.example: The fabric is soft.
items.exampleCN: 织物很柔软。

items.example: The shop sells many fabrics.
items.exampleCN: 这家店卖多种布料。

items.example: They fabricate parts for cars.
items.exampleCN: 他们制造汽车零件。

items.meaning: the act of making or inventing
items.example: The story was a complete fabrication.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事完全是捏造的。

items.meaning: a person who makes or invents things
items.example: The fabricator cut the metal sheets.
items.exampleCN: 制造者切割了金属板。

items.example: Cotton fiber is strong.
items.exampleCN: 棉纤维很结实。

items.example: The textile industry is large.
items.exampleCN: 纺织业规模很大。

items.example: The structure is very old.
items.exampleCN: 这个结构很古老。

items.example: They sat on fabric-covered chairs.
items.exampleCN: 他们坐在覆有织物的椅子上。

latinEntries.example: Faber is the worker behind fabrica.
latinEntries.exampleCN: faber 是 fabrica 背后的工匠。
